article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis dan Tips Pengobatan Sampai Tuntas!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tuberculosis and Tips for Completing Treatment!
article.articleSummary: Indonesia ranks second globally in tuberculosis cases, behind India, and aims to eliminate TB by 2030. The Health Ministry prioritizes TB control and strict treatment monitoring to prevent defaults and transmission, extending care from hospitals to primary health facilities. Pulmonary TB treatment lasts six months uninterrupted; extrapulmonary TB (bone TB, tuberculoma cerebri, TB meningitis, etc.) may require up to 18 months, with evaluation for extension. Diagnosis combines clinical assessment with a rapid molecular test to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum, supported by radiology. TB is airborne, with transmission most likely in enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces, especially in the first two weeks of untreated cough. After diagnosis, patients should discuss duration and adherence with their physician and sign informed consent for medication adherence. An illustrative case describes a 50-year-old man with smoking and diabetes presenting weight loss and productive cough, MTB detected.

article.articleHeadline: Kemenkes masifkan deteksi dini tuberkulosis lewat CKG khusus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health ramps up early tuberculosis detection via specialized CKG.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia's Ministry of Health is ramping up early tuberculosis detection through TB-specific Free Health Checks (Cek Kesehatan Gratis, CKG) in Palu, Central Sulawesi. Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus announced the measure after coordinating TB handling with the Central Sulawesi Provincial Government in Palu on Saturday, August 22, 2026. The TB-focused screenings are conducted under the CKG program, aiming to identify TB cases at earlier stages through targeted health checks. The report provides no TB case counts, laboratory confirmations, or infection sources in this brief, focusing on the policy action and intergovernmental coordination to bolster TB detection efforts in Central Sulawesi.

article.articleHeadline: Bimba morta per difterite, Garattini: "Serve più scienza a scuola. I medici no vax? Sono inaccettabili
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Little girl dies of diphtheria, Garattini: "We need more science in schools. Anti-vax doctors? They are unacceptable."
article.articleSummary: Diphtheria death in Milan, Italy: Anna Rosa Bartolotta, a young girl, dies; her parents are under investigation for manslaughter over alleged failure to vaccinate against the mandatory diphtheria vaccine. A cousin is symptomatic and tested positive for diphtheria but remains not severely ill due to prior vaccination. Professor Silvio Garattini calls for more science in schools and condemns anti-vaccine doctors as unacceptable. He recalls Andrew Wakefield's fraud, noting lasting drops in MMR vaccination and continued measles outbreaks in Europe and the United States. He cites global anti-vaccination episodes—UK 1853 Vaccination Act, Brazil 1904 antivaccination tensions, Nigeria 2003 polio boycott—and warns the Internet and AI could amplify misinformation. Emphasizes clear, evidence-based communication and the simple, essential role of vaccines in preventing deaths like Anna Rosa’s.

triage.headline_ja: ジフテリアで幼児死亡、ガラッティーニ氏「学校でもっと科学教育を。反ワクチン医師は容認できない」
triage.triage_reason: イタリア・ミラノでの単発ジフテリア死亡事例に関する記事であり、対象国（ザンビア、フィリピン等）での発生ではないため対象外。歴史的言及のブラジル・ナイジェリアも現在の発生事例ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はイタリアの未接種家庭における単発ジフテリア死亡例と、それを機にした専門家のワクチン教育に関する論説。ブラジル・ナイジェリア・英国への言及は過去の反ワクチン運動の歴史的事例であり、現在の感染症発生を示すものではない。対象国での発生は確認されず。

article.articleHeadline: Leptospirosis symptoms may appear even after 3 weeks since exposure -- expert
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis cases in Manila surge after flooding from the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat). As of Aug 23, 2026, San Lazaro Hospital has recorded 60 leptospirosis patients since Aug 10, including 22 new admissions and 19 in severe condition, with three deaths. Most cases are linked to wading through floodwaters. Expert Dr. Rontgene Solante warns symptoms may appear up to three weeks after exposure, with incubation as long as about two weeks. Transmission occurs via contact with floodwater contaminated by urine from infected rodents; entry points include open wounds, the eyes, and the mouth. Reported symptoms include fever, vomiting, nausea, muscle pain, and headaches; severe disease can cause jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, and low urine output. Urge to seek medical attention within seven days of symptom onset, and not to delay beyond 24–48 hours. Prevention includes washing the body with soap and water after exposure and seeking prophylaxis.

triage.notes: 洪水後の季節性レプトスピラ症流行であり、フィリピンでは毎年繰り返される事象。60例中3死亡・19重症例と一定の重症度はあるが、ヒト-ヒト感染はなく国際的拡大リスクは低い。続報で死亡者数・重症例数の推移を注視。

article.articleHeadline: Bộ Y tế: Tăng cường giám sát, hạn chế thấp nhất ca tử vong do bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health: Strengthen surveillance to minimize rabies-related deaths.
article.articleSummary: From January to June 2026, Vietnam recorded 34 rabies deaths nationwide, with 23 in the Southern region; Ho Chi Minh City accounted for 5 fatalities in the first six months. To mark World Rabies Day on 28 September 2026, the Ministry of Health’s Preventive Medicine Department urges provincial health authorities to coordinate with veterinary services and implement practical activities, focusing on community and school outreach in high-risk areas and intensified public communications on rabies prevention. Emphasis is on immediate wound washing and seeking medical advice for assessment, post-exposure vaccination, and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). Surveillance should be strengthened to detect and manage exposures, with proper risk assessment, wound care, and PEP. WOAH/OIE notes: 99% of human rabies from dog bites; over 95% of deaths occur in Asia and Africa; rural areas account for >80%; about 4 of 10 deaths in children. Rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear; prevention hinges on early vaccination and avoiding animal bites.

triage.triage_reason: ベトナムにおける狂犬病は既知の風土病であり、本記事は世界狂犬病デーに向けた通常の監視強化・啓発活動の発表であるため、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 狂犬病は致死率がほぼ100%であるため重症度はYesとしたが、本記事は既存の風土病対策の強化に関する定例的な発表であり、シグナルとしての新規性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: 科学网-揭开口蹄疫病毒"劫持"宿主能量的秘密
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: ScienceNet - Unveiling the Secret of How Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus Hijacks Host Energy
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) hijacks host energy metabolism in livestock by activating two autophagy pathways that together boost glycolysis and viral replication. Researchers from the Lanzhou Veterinary Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, China, showed that FMDV simultaneously triggers a selective autophagy route dependent on specific host target proteins and mitophagy, creating a robust metabolic drive for infection. When one pathway is blocked, the other maintains high glycolytic flux, illustrating a dual-pathway safeguard that enhances viral survival in pig, cattle, and sheep cells. Reported in Autophagy and published on 23 August 2026, the work identifies molecular targets within host–autophagy–metabolism crosstalk, offering avenues for host-targeted antiviral strategies and the development of small-molecule therapeutics and new animal disease control agents. This finding underscores a novel mechanism by which FMDV leverages host energy systems to sustain propagation, relevant to global livestock health.

triage.headline_ja: 科学网-揭开口蹄疫病毒「劫持」宿主能量的秘密（ScienceNet - 口蹄疫病毒が宿主エネルギーをハイジャックするメカニズムの解明）
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は口蹄疫病毒の分子メカニズムに関する基礎研究論文の報告であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクではなく、疾病流行の兆候を示すイベント情報ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は中国の蘭州獣医研究所による基礎研究論文（Autophagy誌掲載）の報告であり、実際のアウトブレイク情報ではない。口蹄疫の分子生物学的メカニズム研究について学術的に報告しているもので、感染症危機管理のシグナルトリアージの対象外。Bluedot APIが誤ったコンテキストで疾患名を抽出したと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Конго получило более 16 тысяч доз вакцины на фоне самой стремительной вспышки Эболы в истории
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo received more than 16,000 doses of vaccine amid the fastest Ebola outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo faces the fastest Ebola outbreak in history, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. In six provinces, 5,375 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths have been reported. The outbreak spreads rapidly, with officials warning transmission has not yet peaked and contact tracing is overwhelmed; symptoms can resemble malaria, complicating detection. The Ervebo vaccine (rVSV-ZEBOV) has begun deployment: Congo received 16,250 doses, part of a plan to deliver 70,000 doses, with additional shipments expected early next week. The first batch arrived at N'djili International Airport in Kinshasa on August 22. There is no approved treatment or vaccine specifically for Bundibugyo; Ervebo may offer some protection. The response is hindered by armed conflict, attacks on health workers and facilities, and population displacement, complicating outbreak control.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、史上最速のエボラ流行の中、1万6千回分以上のワクチンを受領
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速とされるエボラ流行で6州に拡大し、5,375例確認・2,557死亡と甚大な公衆衛生への影響があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルスによる史上最速の流行とされ、6州に拡大、致死率約47.6%。武装紛争や医療従事者への攻撃、住民の避難民化が対応を困難にしている。マラリアと症状が類似し検知が複雑化している点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Shigellosis cases open up a new AMR challenge in Keralam
article.articleSummary: Shigellosis in Keralam faces rising antimicrobial resistance, with primary antibiotics for community-acquired cases losing efficacy. KARS-Net data (since 2023) show ciprofloxacin resistance at 96% and ceftriaxone resistance at 36%. Community-acquired AMR now concerns treatment outside hospitals. Clinicians warn that shrinking antibiotic options jeopardizes management of severe dysentery, where patients may progress to septic shock or multiorgan failure; ceftriaxone may be unreliable, forcing consideration of meropenem in critical cases. Shigella transmission remains food- and water-borne, making it a sentinel AMR indicator for community trends. A major outbreak in June this year tallied 225 cases and six deaths across Kozhikode, Malappuram and Wayanad. Keralam has historical ESBL-producing strains and prior MDR patterns; a 2018 Government Medical College Alappuzha study reported 91.6% MDR among isolates and Ceftriaxone/Cefotaxime resistance. Most diarrhoea is self-limiting, but vulnerable groups require antibiotics.

triage.headline_ja: ケララ州でシゲラ症例が新たな薬剤耐性(AMR)の課題を提起
triage.triage_reason: ケララ州で225例・6死亡の大規模シゲラ症アウトブレイクが発生し、シプロフロキサシン耐性96%など深刻な多剤耐性の進行が確認されており、公衆衛生上の懸念とAMRという異常性からIHR基準を2つ以上満たす。
triage.notes: KARS-Net（Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network）のデータに基づくAMR動向報告。2025年6月にKozhikode、Malappuram、Wayanadで225例・6死亡の大規模アウトブレイクが発生。国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候はないが、community-acquired AMRの進行は公衆衛生上重要な監視対象。

article.articleHeadline: Конго отримало понад 16 тисяч доз вакцини на тлі найшвидшого спалаху Еболи в історії
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has received more than 16,000 doses of vaccine amid the fastest Ebola outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-23, the Democratic Republic of the Congo received 16,250 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine amid an unprecedented Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak. Six provinces report 5,375 confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths. The first vaccine batch arrived late Aug 22 at N'Djili International Airport in Kinshasa; the WHO and partners aim to deploy about 70,000 doses, with additional shipments expected early next week. Bundibugyo has no approved treatment or vaccine; Ervebo is licensed for Ebola virus disease and has shown effectiveness in prior outbreaks, with WHO indicating it may offer some protection against Bundibugyo. The outbreak is expanding rapidly, described as the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the region, as health workers struggle to conduct contact tracing amid armed conflict, attacks on medical facilities, population displacement, and weakened infrastructure. This vaccination effort is part of the international response to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴが史上最速のエボラ流行の中、1万6千回分以上のワクチンを受領
triage.triage_reason: DRCでブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスによる過去最悪規模の流行が発生し、確認症例5,375人・死者2,557人と深刻な公衆衛生への影響があり、武力紛争下での対応困難や国際的なワクチン支援が行われているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 承認されたブンディブギョ株用の治療薬・ワクチンが存在しない中、Ervebo（本来はザイールエボラウイルス用）を使用する試みであり、有効性は未確定。武力紛争下での接触者追跡困難、医療施設への攻撃、住民の避難等が流行拡大の要因となっている。

article.articleHeadline: В Конго доставили первую партию вакцины от Эболы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The first batch of Ebola vaccine has been delivered to Congo.
article.articleSummary: First batch of Ebola vaccine Ervebo delivered to the Democratic Republic of Congo to help respond to an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain. Kinshasa received 16,250 doses of 70,000 planned; another shipment expected early next week. Delivery organized by WHO and partners. No vaccine specifically approved for this variant yet, but WHO expects Ervebo to offer some protection; the vaccine has proven effectiveness in prior outbreaks. As of latest data, DRC confirms 5,375 cases and 2,557 deaths; authorities call it the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. Transmission is complicated by armed conflict, attacks on health workers, and population displacement; Africa CDC warns the peak may not yet be reached and cases could rise significantly.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにエボラワクチンの第一便が到着
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（5,375症例、2,557人死亡）が継続しており、ワクチン投入や国際支援が行われている重大な公衆衛生事象のため。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による流行で、既承認ワクチンがない点、武力紛争・住民避難により対応が複雑化している点、Africa CDCがピーク未到達を警告している点が特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: '8 Out Of 10 Positive': Inside Delhi-NCR's H1N1 Hospital Wards
article.articleSummary: Delhi-NCR is contending with a sharp fever surge mainly driven by H1N1 (Influenza A). Hospital reporting shows high positivity: Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, about eight of ten tested are positive for Influenza A/H1N1; recent OPD rounds show 15–16 of 20 positive; Fortis Faridabad similarly notes 60–70% positivity among flu-like cases. Delhi has recorded at least seven times more H1N1 cases this year than the same period last year (NCDC). The surge began earlier than usual (last 15 days to one month) with high-grade fever, sore throat, and cough, and a growing number developing pneumonia requiring hospitalization (roughly half of positives). Some cases progress to H1N1-related pneumonia; possible changes in circulating strains or environmental factors are under study. Vaccination is reinforced as the best protection. Notable patient example includes a 39-year-old with H1N1-related pneumonia and evidence of household transmission patterns.

triage.headline_ja: 「10人中8人が陽性」：デリーNCRのH1N1病棟の実情
triage.triage_reason: デリーNCRでH1N1の症例が例年比7倍に急増し、陽性者の約半数が肺炎で入院するなど重症化傾向が見られ、IHR基準を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: NCDCデータによる前年比7倍の増加、通常より早い流行開始、家庭内感染の証拠、陽性者の約半数が肺炎を発症するなど重症度・異常性の両面で懸念が高い。季節性インフルエンザではあるが規模と重症度が例年と異なる点に注意。

article.articleHeadline: 'Wear masks, avoid crowds': Delhi steps up surveillance as H1N1 cases cross 1,777- Moneycontrol.com
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 2,602 influenza cases in 2026 so far, with 2,392 Influenza-A and 210 Influenza-B; H1N1 remains the predominant Influenza-A subtype with 1,777 cases, followed by H3 and H1 subtypes. 114 new H1N1 infections were recorded on Thursday, adding to rising activity as the capital strengthens surveillance. 35 hospitals are under special surveillance; AIIMS and the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) are referral laboratories for testing and monitoring. A public health advisory urges masks in crowded places, respiratory hygiene, cough etiquette, handwashing, and prompt medical consultation for flu-like symptoms. Technical guidelines cover patient categorisation, home-based care, ventilatory support and mask use; facilities are directed to enhance screening and reporting via the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP). IDSP tracks surveillance; authorities claim adequate resources and no bed shortages. Delhi faces expected seasonal peaks; H1N1 currently dominates in Delhi, with H3N2 leading in 2025.

article.articleHeadline: 16 Unit Portable X-Ray Segera Tiba di Sulteng, Perkuat Deteksi Dini Kasus TB
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sixteen Portable X-ray Units to Arrive Soon in Central Sulawesi, to Bolster Early Detection of TB Cases.
article.articleSummary: Sixteen portable X-ray units will arrive in September 2026 to bolster early detection of tuberculosis (TB) in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. The initiative supports the Sulawesi Tengah provincial government’s target of TB elimination by 2030 and is backed by the Ministry of Health. Governor Anwar Hafid announced the plan during a visit by senior ministry officials on August 22, 2026, stating that easier access to screening will help identify cases sooner and accelerate treatment initiation. Beyond equipment, the province plans district- and city-level TB Task Forces and a provincial TB Task Force to monitor and evaluate program implementation across regencies. Officials stress cross-district coordination as essential to reducing TB burden, noting that TB cases in Central Sulawesi remain high. No specific case numbers or laboratory-confirmed data are provided.

article.articleSummary: Swine flu (H1N1) is rising in Delhi and the Delhi-NCR region. Typical symptoms include fever, runny nose or cough, body aches, and fatigue. As of 12 August 2026, Delhi has recorded 1,449 H1N1 infections, about six times higher than 229 cases at the same point last year, according to the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC). Medical professionals say monsoon humidity is intensifying transmission. In response, major hospitals have begun special preparations to manage the surge. The report underscores vigilance for flu-like illness and notes the outbreak's ongoing spread in Delhi and adjacent areas, with emphasis on early diagnosis, appropriate care, and reporting through public health channels.

article.articleHeadline: 한 달 새 52만명 폭발"... 중국 덮친 코로나19 재확산, 한국도 '비상'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 520,000 people infected in a month: COVID-19 resurgence sweeps through China, South Korea on high alert.
article.articleSummary: China experiences a COVID-19 resurgence, with July reported new confirmed cases reaching 522,000. Among those with influenza-like illness seeking outpatient or emergency care, COVID-19 positivity rose to 21.2% for five consecutive weeks. In Korea, the second week of August (Aug 9–15) COVID-19 detection was 9.1%, up about 2.8-fold from 3.2% three weeks earlier. Taiwan reports rising cases and temporary vaccine shortages in some areas due to increased demand. Experts warn that outbreak size is hard to predict and stress proactive vaccine stockpiling and continued personal protective measures. They referenced last year when early vaccination campaigns failed to reach high-risk elderly populations, contributing to vaccine depletion in some cases. The situation underscores the need for coordinated vaccine supply management and adherence to protective practices to mitigate a potential broader regional surge.

triage.headline_ja: 「一ヶ月で52万人急増」...中国を襲うコロナ再拡大、韓国も『非常事態』
triage.triage_reason: 中国・台湾・韓国で同時にCOVID-19感染が急増しており、地域的拡大とワクチン供給への懸念、社会的関心の高さからWPRO基準複数該当かつ社会的注目もあるためフルリスク評価へ進める。
triage.notes: 台湾・韓国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。COVID-19の季節的再流行として季節性が疑われるが、感染規模とワクチン不足の報告から注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Swine Flu Cases: Over 2,300 Influenza-A cases reported; what people should know about the latest health advisory
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports rising swine flu (H1N1) cases with a health advisory urging respiratory hygiene and avoidance of crowded places. As of Friday, Delhi has logged 2,602 influenza cases this year: 2,392 Influenza-A (1,777 H1N1; 37 H1; 138 H3; 440 other Influenza-A) and 210 Influenza-B (200 Victoria, 10 others). On Thursday alone, 155 Influenza-A cases were recorded (114 H1N1; 2 H1; 1 H3; 38 other Influenza-A) and 4 Influenza-B. H1N1 dominates Delhi’s influenza tally this year; the capital is preparing with 35 hospitals under special surveillance, AIIMS and NCDC labs designated for testing, and technical guidelines for treatment, ventilation, masks, and home care. Daily monitoring via IDSP-IHIP, with surveillance, reporting, and awareness campaigns across departments; vulnerable groups include young children and the elderly with comorbidities.

triage.headline_ja: デリーの豚インフルエンザ（H1N1）症例：インフルエンザA型症例2,300件超を報告、最新の健康勧告について知っておくべきこと

triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの増加事例。重症度（死亡者数・重症例の割合）に関する具体的記載がなく不明。デリー市当局は自国内で対応中で、国際的な支援要請の記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: OPAKI VIRUS SE OTRGAO KONTROLI! Preti da nadmaši najsmrtonosniju epidemiju ikada zabeleženu, lekari se bore da zaustave zarazu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A deadly virus has spiraled out of control! It threatens to surpass the deadliest epidemic ever recorded, and doctors are fighting to contain the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo is battling the most severe Ebola outbreak in its history, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. As of August 23, 2026, 5,290 laboratory-confirmed cases have produced 2,516 deaths. The epidemic is spreading rapidly and risks surpassing the deadliest West Africa outbreak (2014–2016) which killed over 11,000 people. Transmission is not yet peaked and could triple in rate. Some symptoms resemble malaria, complicating detection. Campaigns continue to deploy vaccines: a shipment of Ervebo—over 16,000 doses arrived in Kinshasa, with more expected next week, and the World Health Organization anticipates about 70,000 doses in total for the response. Ervebo is licensed for Ebola and may provide some protection against Bundibugyo virus, though there is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for this strain. Armed conflict and healthcare disruption hinder control efforts.

triage.headline_ja: 凶悪なウイルスが制御不能に！ 史上最悪の致死的流行を超える恐れ、医師たちは感染拡大の阻止に奮闘
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最大規模とされるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の流行が急拡大しており、致死率も高く国際的関心・支援の必要性が極めて高い。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及されておらず、対象国リストにも該当しないため除外。ブンディブギョ株には承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、既存のErvebo接種のみで対応している点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: ''중국 코로나 재유행?'' 한 달 52만 명 확진...한국도 3주 만에 2.8배↑
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "China's COVID-19 resurgence?" 520,000 confirmed cases in one month... Korea also up 2.8-fold in three weeks.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, China reports a COVID-19 resurgence: July's new confirmed cases exceed 522,000 with 487 severe cases and 1 death. Sentinel surveillance from 1,041 hospitals shows influenza-like illness patients testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 at 21.2% between July 27 and August 2, a 13-point rise in five weeks. Despite rising indicators, most cases are mild, and Chinese authorities do not characterize it as a pandemic-scale spread. In South Korea, COVID-19 indicators rise: detection rate among respiratory samples is 9.1% in week 33 (Aug 9–15) across 106 facilities; hospitalizations reach 56 in week 33, a 2.4-fold increase from week 30. Taiwan also experiences temporary vaccine shortages amid spread; the article cautions vigilance for regional transmission and stresses vaccine stock management to ensure elderly uptake.

triage.headline_ja: 「中国でコロナ再流行？」1か月で52万人感染確認…韓国も3週間で2.8倍増

triage.notes: 重症例・死亡例は少なく、中国当局もパンデミック規模とは認識していないが、複数国での同時的な検出率上昇はモニタリングに値する。台湾のワクチン供給不足にも留意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 'I couldn't even complete a sentence': Cancer survivor battles Swine Flu amid Delhi surge
article.articleSummary: H1N1 influenza (swine flu) is causing a sharp Delhi surge as of August 2026. 30-year-old Tabarigum, undergoing induction chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia at Apollo Hospital Jasola, tested positive for H1N1 after presenting with a fever, cough, and respiratory symptoms; his leukocyte and absolute neutrophil counts were very low, necessitating five days in isolation. He has since recovered and was discharged, returning to Arunachal Pradesh. Delhi reports 1,777 H1N1 cases this year, with 114 new cases on August 20, and 2,392 total Influenza-A infections, prompting health authorities to review hospital preparedness and issue prevention/treatment advisories. Early antiviral treatment with oseltamivir and vaccination are emphasized; immunocompromised patients, including those on chemotherapy, face higher risk of severe influenza, pneumonia, and potential multi-organ dysfunction. Key guidance includes early testing, prompt medical contact, and preventive measures such as masks and hygiene.

triage.headline_ja: 「一文も話せなかった」:デリーでのH1N1感染拡大の中、がん生存者がスワインフルーと闘う

triage.notes: 季節性H1N1インフルエンザの症例数増加（デリーで年間1,777例、8月20日に114例新規）。免疫不全（化学療法中）患者での重症化例が報告されているが、既知の病原体による季節性流行であり国際的緊急性は低い。地元当局が病院準備体制を見直している点は注目される。

article.articleHeadline: エボラ感染拡大のコンゴ、人口1700万の首都で高まる警戒と水際対策
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo raises vigilance and border-control measures in Kinshasa, the capital with a population of 17 million.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo prompts heightened vigilance and border controls in Kinshasa, a city of about 17 million. At the Mark District port, 70 km northeast of Kinshasa, liaison officers use loudspeakers to direct passengers arriving by boat from higher‑risk areas. Hundreds arrive daily by wooden boats from the north and east; Kinshasa has not yet reported cases, but authorities are tightening screening on arrival. A worker wearing a 'Stop Ebola' shirt says arrivals from high‑risk regions undergo testing and may be detained if needed. Kisangani, a major northeast river city, has sent three boats; about 15 infections have been recorded there since May 15. Nationwide, more than 2,500 deaths after roughly 100 days, with about half confirmed in the last three weeks. Six provinces report around 5,000 cases, though officials fear many more undetected infections. Screening includes temperature and symptom checks; boats are disinfected by teams in full PPE. Incubation is 2–21 days.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ感染拡大のコンゴ、人口1700万の首都で高まる警戒と水際対策
triage.triage_reason: DRCで国全体死者2,500人超・6州で約5,000症例という大規模エボラ流行が継続中で、人口1700万の首都キンシャサへの拡大リスクが高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 首都キンシャサでは未だ症例未確認だが、北東部からの船舶到着者への検疫強化中。全国で100日間に2,500人超死亡、6州で約5,000症例、未検出感染者が多数存在する懸念あり。継続的なモニタリングとフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Gejala Infeksi Virus Zika yang Perlu Dikenali
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Symptoms of Zika Virus Infection That Need to Be Recognized
article.articleSummary: Zika virus infection is typically mild, and hospitalization is rare. Do not use nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen until dengue is ruled out due to bleeding risk. Medical evaluation should be sought if symptoms worsen or there is possible Zika exposure, especially for pregnant individuals. Zika infection during pregnancy can be transmitted to the fetus and cause serious complications even when the mother has mild or no symptoms. In rare cases, Zika is linked to neurological complications like Guillain-Barré syndrome, which can cause weakness and potentially progress to paralysis; any new or worsening neurological symptoms after infection require prompt medical assessment. Guidance comes from the World Health Organization and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, supported by clinical studies on Zika manifestations.

triage.headline_ja: 認識すべきジカウイルス感染症の症状

triage.notes: 記事は一般的な医療解説であり、インドネシアにおける具体的な発生・流行を報じるものではないため、verified_locationsは空とする。

article.articleHeadline: Réception à Kinshasa des premières doses de vaccin RVBO contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kinshasa receives the first doses of the RVBO vaccine against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa received the first doses of the RVBO Ebola vaccine, financed by Gavi, with 16,520 doses arriving at N'djili International Airport on Friday, August 21, 2026. The shipment is part of a planned delivery totaling 50,120 doses expected between August 21–24 to bolster the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola response. Manufactured in Germany by MSD, the vaccines transited via Switzerland, Luxembourg and Belgium before reaching Kinshasa. Health Minister Dr. Samuel Roger Kamba announced the arrival, noting the deployment aims to protect populations and reinforce the government's outbreak response with international partner support. Further shipments are expected through August 24, and this stock aligns with the government's strategy to scale up vaccination coverage in response to Ebola risk.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola im Kongo: Trauer, Trauma, Stigma - Ebola-Waisen im Kongo - Panorama - Rhein-Zeitung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Kongo: Grief, Trauma, Stigma - Ebola orphans in the Kongo - Panorama - Rhein-Zeitung.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Kongo region, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, has claimed more than 2,500 lives. The African health authority notes that the pediatric fatality is exceptionally high: two-thirds of infected children under one year die, and 58.5% of those aged 1–4, with an overall population fatality around 47.5%. UNICEF estimates children aged 0–17 comprise about 20% of confirmed infections. At least 180 children have become orphans since the outbreak was announced roughly 100 days ago. Stigmatization and trauma accompany bereavement, including social exclusion and separation during isolation. Save the Children is establishing dedicated observation and care centers to provide medical, psychosocial, and protective support. Contact tracing remains challenging in distrustful communities, highlighting the need for early detection to improve survival.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱：悲しみ、トラウマ、スティグマ ― コンゴのエボラ孤児たち
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で2,500人以上が死亡する大規模なエボラ流行が継続中であり、致死率が極めて高く（全体約47.5%、乳幼児では約67%）、国際的な支援機関（UNICEF、Save the Children）が介入している点からPICKUPと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ東部（Kongo地域）における進行中のエボラ流行に関するもので、致死率の高さ・孤児問題・スティグマなど社会的影響が強調されている。国際的な感染拡大や渡航制限の有無については記事内で明示されていないため不明とした。

article.articleSummary: As of August 23, 2026, Punjab has 93 confirmed H1N1 (swine flu) infections since late July, with Ludhiana district accounting for the majority. Reports from Ludhiana’s Dayanand Medical College and Hospital and Patiala’s Government Rajindra Hospital note a rise in feverish, viral illnesses; medical care is advised for persistent or severe symptoms.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo receives first batch of Ebola vaccines; will evaluate effectiveness | International
article.articleSummary: DR Congo receives the first batch of Ebola vaccines (Ervebo) to address the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak; Ervebo is approved for Zaire ebolavirus, with unclear protection against Bundibugyo. On Aug 21, Kinshasa received 16,520 doses; total deliveries of 50,120 planned by Aug 24. The WHO has allocated 70,000 doses: 20,000 for a phase 3 trial to evaluate protection against Bundibugyo and 50,000 for frontline health workers. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there is no strain-specific vaccine or therapy yet, though early laboratory and animal data suggest potential protection from Ervebo. As of Aug 19, cumulative cases reach 5,290, deaths 2,516, and recoveries 1,152. About 160 healthcare workers have been infected, 43 of whom have died. The epicenter is Bunia in Ituri province, with ongoing security/access challenges complicating outbreak control.

article.articleHeadline: Роспотребнадзор отслеживает данные о вспышке легионеллёза в Австрии
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rospotrebnadzor tracks data on a Legionellosis outbreak in Austria.
article.articleSummary: Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in the Linz area, Austria, involves 26 cases and 3 deaths. Rospotrebnadzor is monitoring the situation and evaluating overseas risks. Legionella pneumophila was detected in a cooling system and subsequently cleaned and disinfected; the source is not yet confirmed as exclusive. Transmission occurs via inhalation of water aerosols from hot-water systems, pools, water parks, and centralized air-conditioning. Diagnostics use PCR tests from TsNIIP Epi (Rospotrebnadzor); Russian hygiene centers monitor cold- and hot-water systems, with hot-water temperatures kept at ≥60°C to suppress growth. Preventive measures include regular cleaning/disinfection and avoiding water stagnation. The article also references the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo: 5,290 cases, 2,516 deaths; WHO plans 70,000 Ervebo vaccine doses, with 50,000 for hotspots and 20,000 for Bundibugyo ebolavirus trials.

article.articleHeadline: Lampaui Target Nasional, Banten Jadi Contoh CKG-TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Surpassing the National Target, Banten Becomes an Example of CKG-TBC
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, Banten Province, especially Tangerang Regency, surpassed the national target in Free Health Check (CKG) and TB case finding, becoming a national model. Health Ministry data show CKG coverage at 5,934,010 people (100.60% of target), among the top provinces. TB case finding exceeded the estimated burden at 112%, with TB treatment success at 91%. The program benefits from integrated service delivery and cross-sector collaboration, including portable X-ray in CKG to speed detection of pulmonary abnormalities and to connect with hypertension and diabetes screening. Plans include 16 portable X-ray units via APBN 2026 across eight districts in Banten. Andra Soni says the province aims to enroll more than half of residents in CKG; Tangerang Regency is about 46% complete. National target is 130 million by 2026; current coverage is ~82 million. Citizens are urged to use CKG at local facilities to cut transmission and detect risks early.

article.articleHeadline: Deja más de 2,500 mu3rtos brote de ébol@ en República Democrática del Congo - Medios OBSON
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo leaves more than 2,500 dead - OBSON Media
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 2,500 deaths about 100 days after declaration. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (Bundibugyo virus), a rare Ebola strain with no approved treatment or vaccine. It spreads rapidly and can go undetected because its symptoms resemble those of other illnesses. The overall case fatality rate is about 46.7%, rising to 68.2% in North Kivu, one of the most populous provinces at the epicenter. Containment is hindered by ongoing armed conflict between the government and rebel groups controlling key cities. The situation could surpass Africa’s deadliest outbreak (2014–2016) in West Africa, which caused more than 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、死者2,500人超に - OBSON Media
triage.triage_reason: 希少株（ブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス）による大規模流行で死者2,500人超、致死率約47〜68%、武力紛争により封じ込めが困難であり、国際的関心・支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリー本文はDRC（特に北キブ州）における流行のみを記述しており、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬未承認の希少株（ブンディブギョ株）であり、武力紛争が対応を妨げている点が特に懸念材料。

article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, Delhi has recorded over 2,300 Influenza-A cases this year, including more than 1,777 H1N1 (swine flu) cases, with 114 H1N1 cases reported on Thursday. Of Influenza-A, 1,777 are H1N1, 37 H1, 138 H3, and 440 other; Influenza-B includes 200 Victoria strain and 10 other cases. Health experts warn H1N1 cases are six times higher than the previous year and are notably severe, though symptoms largely mirror seasonal flu (fever, cough, sore throat, body aches); elderly and those with comorbidities are at greater risk, with potential progression to pneumonia. No mortality linked to H1N1 reported in OPD so far. The Delhi government issued a respiratory hygiene advisory (masks in crowded places, hand hygiene, avoid close contact), while Union Health Minister JP Nadda chaired a national review of surveillance and preparedness, noting need for vigilance and antivirals where appropriate.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alarming swine flu outbreak in Delhi; hospitals have reserved beds; learn the symptoms and preventive measures.
article.articleSummary: Swine flu (H1N1) outbreak in Delhi escalates: 135 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the total to 1,912. Hospitals have expanded capacity: DDU Hospital opened a fever clinic with a 70-bed fever ward and an 8-bed isolation ward; GTB Hospital in Yamuna Par has 10 beds reserved. Most patients are treated symptomatically with paracetamol, anti-allergic drugs, ORS, IV fluids, and antibiotics for sputum cough when needed. About 10% of emergency patients present with fever. Private hospitals offer tele-consultations for home care. Preventive measures include regular handwashing, avoiding face touching, rest, coconut water, ORS, and warm soup; annual influenza vaccine reduces severity and hospitalization risk. Red flags: blue lips, persistent cough after 4–5 days, lethargy or confusion, reduced urine in children, or fever not subsiding after 48 hours; H1N1 fever tends to stay high. Dr. Vinod Kumar (GTB) notes 5–7% risk of severe infection; most care is at OPD.

article.articleHeadline: Swine flu in Delhi: Govt lists H1N1 symptoms; know causes, treatment, and prevention
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports a rising wave of H1N1/swine flu with over 1,700 confirmed cases this year, as of 23 August 2026, prompting heightened surveillance. H1N1 is an Influenza A strain now treated as part of seasonal influenza; transmission occurs mainly via respiratory droplets and close contact, with crowded indoor spaces facilitating spread. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, body aches, fatigue, diarrhea, and loss of appetite; symptoms can resemble other viral infections, so testing may be advised. Higher risk groups are older adults, very young children, pregnant people, and those with underlying conditions. Most cases recover with rest and fluids; antivirals may be prescribed for higher-risk or more severe illness. Prevention emphasizes good hygiene, masking in crowded settings, staying home when unwell, and seasonal influenza vaccination for high-risk individuals.

article.articleHeadline: Swine Flu Cases Spike Across India: Health Ministry Lists Common Symptoms To Watch For
article.articleSummary: Swine flu (H1N1) is the dominant influenza strain this season in India, with Delhi and Mumbai among cities reporting rising cases. Delhi has logged 1,777 H1N1 cases this year within 2,392 Influenza A infections, prompting a review by Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh. Laboratories report increased demand for testing as respiratory symptoms appear. The Health Ministry lists common H1N1 symptoms: fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, body/muscle pain, fatigue, with possible nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, lethargy, and loss of appetite. Most recover within about a week, though cough can persist. WHO notes influenza can cause severe illness in high-risk groups. High-risk: young children, older adults, pregnant women, chronic conditions; healthcare workers at greater exposure. Testing is advised based on condition, risk factors, and local activity; seek care for persistent or worsening symptoms and avoid self-medication.

article.articleSummary: Delhi reports a rising H1N1 (swine flu) surge within a broader influenza spike, with 2,602 influenza cases this year: 2,392 influenza-A and 210 influenza-B. Of influenza-A, 1,777 are H1N1, including 114 new H1N1 cases on Thursday; other influenza-A cases include 2 H1, 1 H3, and 38 non-H1N1. A public health advisory urges mask use in crowded places, strict respiratory hygiene, regular handwashing, avoiding touching eyes/nose, not spitting in public, and staying hydrated; seek medical advice for fever, cough, sore throat, shortness of breath, body aches, or headaches rather than self-medicating. article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Butembo : les jeunes de Kasesa-Kyahala s'engagent dans la
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Butembo: the youth of Kasesa-Kyahala are engaging in the.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, Ebola response efforts in Butembo (Nord Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo) receive renewed community support from the youth of the Kasesa-Kyahala neighborhood in the Bulengera commune. After previous resistance to sensitization, the Butembo Youth Parliament facilitated sessions that helped shift attitudes, with the majority of youths now pledging to cooperate with health teams and help relay prevention messages. The initiative emphasizes mutual forgiveness between frontline workers and youths and involves local leaders—community chiefs and neighborhood authorities—to bolster trust. The youth parliament plans to extend sensitization to other zones facing similar resistance. Health authorities reiterate that winning community trust is essential to preventing new Ebola transmissions, making social mobilization a critical pillar of the ongoing outbreak response in the region.

article.articleSummary: Rabies-transmitting animals in West Jakarta are being vaccinated by the city’s Food Security, Maritime Affairs and Agriculture Office (KPKP). On 19 August, 36 animals in RW 005 Jelambar, Grogol Petamburan were vaccinated: 23 dogs, 12 cats, and 1 monkey, as part of a vaccination drive to curb rabies risk. The campaign is proactive outreach (jemput bola) to raise household vaccination awareness and keep Jelambar free from rabies. Nurul Indri Hapsari, head of Jelambar’s Community Welfare Section, said the free rabies vaccination helps residents protect their pets while saving time and costs; vaccination is a preventive measure. The effort highlights ongoing public health measures in West Jakarta to prevent rabies transmission from companion animals to humans through routine vaccination.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swine flu risk increasing in Delhi! Doctor warns about H1N1; do not ignore these symptoms.
article.articleSummary: Swine flu (H1N1) risk is rising in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). In July–August this year, Delhi/NCR reported 1,777 H1N1 cases, up from 229 in the same period last year (2025). Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, fatigue and weakness, affecting mainly the nose, throat and lungs. Most recover with rest and appropriate treatment, but severe cases can cause dehydration, low oxygen levels, and added strain on the heart. Myocarditis—inflammation of the heart muscle—has been associated with the infection. High-risk groups include the elderly and people with pre-existing heart disease or hypertension. Warning signs warranting medical attention: chest pain or pressure, breathlessness, very rapid or irregular heartbeat, sudden weakness, dizziness, or excessive sweating. Seek prompt medical care; avoid unnecessary panic, but do not ignore symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Gurugram reports three fresh dengue cases, season tally reaches 29
article.articleSummary: Gurugram reported three dengue cases on Saturday, raising the season tally to 29. The health department cited monsoon-related stagnation in low-lying areas and has stepped up surveillance, including fever surveys and testing. Saturday saw 357 dengue samples collected, bringing the total to 6,848, with no dengue deaths so far. Mass fever surveys covered 10,267 houses, pushing cumulative coverage to over 1.01 million. 835 blood slides were prepared for malaria surveillance, with four malaria cases reported this year. Authorities issued 1,485 notices under Section 214 of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act to curb mosquito breeding, urging residents to eliminate standing water in coolers, pots, rooftops, and other water-collection points. Sectors 9A, 10, Udyog Vihar, MG Road, and Sadar Bazar report persistent stagnation; residents say pumps or tankers have not been provided. In 2025, Gurugram recorded 64 dengue cases with zero fatalities.

article.articleSummary: Awareness rally led by Mukhiya Sujata Hansda in Galudih's Marshy Panchayat to prevent malaria and dengue. article.articleHeadline: Najbolj smrtonosen izbruh ebole v zgodovini kosi življenja - je ogrožena tudi Evropa?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in history is taking lives — is Europe also at risk?
article.articleSummary: Ebola, Bundibugyo strain, is causing the region’s deadliest outbreak, centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda. By August 2026, the outbreak has killed over 2,300 people (UN official Julien Harneis cites more than 2,500) with nearly 5,000 cases reported. There are no approved antivirals or vaccines for Bundibugyo, unlike Zaire ebolavirus. International efforts are advancing clinical trials of experimental antivirals and vaccine candidates, with ring vaccination planned once a safe and effective candidate is identified. The crisis is exacerbated by armed conflict, community distrust, misinformation, and severely weak health infrastructure that hinder access; more than 1,000 people have recovered. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of symptomatic individuals; it is not airborne. European risk is deemed very low by ECDC/WHO, though travel-related introductions may occur. The best defense is rapid response and sustained support to the affected African countries.

Ongoing surveillance and hospital readiness are emphasized to manage the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Seasonal flu shot can also protect against H1N1, the virus behind swine flu
article.articleSummary: Seasonal influenza now includes the H1N1 component (A(H1N1)pdm09), alongside H3N2 and influenza B, reflecting its ongoing human circulation since the 2009 emergence. In India, Delhi is a rising hotspot with 1,777 H1N1 cases reported by August 20 and 114 new cases in a day; total Delhi influenza cases reach 2,602 (2,392 Influenza-A, 210 Influenza-B). Health authorities issued a flu advisory and heightened hospital preparedness as the Union Health Minister reviewed the situation. For 2026-27, WHO’s northern-hemisphere recommendation includes an H1N1pdm09-like strain in egg-based and cell culture/recombinant vaccines. Vaccination primes the immune system, taking about two weeks to develop protective antibodies and reducing the risk of influenza and severe outcomes, though it is not a guarantee against infection. Typical H1N1 symptoms include fever, sore throat, cough, body aches, fatigue, with potential progression to pneumonia or respiratory failure.

article.articleSummary: As of August 23, 2026, China reports 522,000 new COVID-19 cases last month, with 487 severe cases and 1 death. In Korea, week 33 of the respiratory virus survey (Aug 9–15) found COVID-19 positivity at 9.1% across 106 institutions, up from 3.2% in week 30 and 5.7% the prior week, about a 2.8-fold rise. Taiwan reports rising infections and temporary COVID-19 vaccine stockouts in some areas. Experts warn the summer surge is unpredictable, emphasizing protection of older and high-risk groups, monitoring vaccine supplies, and maintaining hand hygiene and ventilation to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Containment of the African swine fever outbreak in the largest pig farming area in the eastern part of Ho Chi Minh City.
article.articleSummary: Two African swine fever outbreaks have been recorded in Xuan Son commune, the largest pig-farming area in eastern Ho Chi Minh City, since January 2026. Authorities report containment efforts in this high-density area, with weather fluctuations—alternating sun and rain—potentially aiding spread. Farmers are urged to monitor pigs for sudden high fever, loss of appetite, hemorrhages, weakness, or unexplained death and to promptly notify local authorities or veterinary officers; home treatment or concealing infections is strongly discouraged. Infected herds are culled to prevent further transmission, and strict hygiene measures prevent movement of pigs with unclear origin. Farmers should not purchase, transport, slaughter, or receive pigs of unknown provenance; avoid disposing of dead pigs in the environment. While a vaccine exists, there is no specific treatment; proactive biosecurity, surveillance, rapid reporting, and adherence to control measures remain essential.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市東部最大の養豚地域でアフリカ豚熱の発生を処理
triage.triage_reason: 動物疾病（アフリカ豚熱）であり人への健康影響はなく、既知の疾病で管理体制も機能しているためフルRRAの対象外。
triage.notes: アフリカ豚熱は人獣共通感染症ではなく、動物（豚）のみに影響する疾病。地方当局による通常の防疫対応が行われており、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Puluhan Unggas Warga di Panton Reu Mati Mendadak, Wabah Aratan Resahkan Peternak
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dozens of residents' poultry in Panton Reu die suddenly; Aratan outbreak unsettles farmers.
article.articleSummary: In Aceh Barat Regency, Aceh Province, Indonesia, dozens of poultry in Gampong Tamping (Tamping Village), Panton Reu District, have died suddenly over several days amid a local outbreak described as kunyang or aratan. The suspected disease is Newcastle Disease (ND), though authorities have yet to confirm via laboratory testing. Individual losses include Susi (3), Chacha (5), Liana (4), Roshani (3), and Alvi (6), with many households reporting multiple deaths as nearly all poultry keepers are affected. Affected birds become lethargic, lose appetite, and die quickly. Residents fear the outbreak will spread before upcoming Pang Ule celebrations for Maulid Nabi Muhammad SAW. Community members call on the district government and relevant agencies to inspect and implement preventive measures to halt further spread and protect livelihoods and household consumption.

triage.headline_ja: パントンレウ地区の住民が飼育する多数の家禽が突然死、『アラタン』の流行で養鶏農家が不安に
triage.triage_reason: 家禽(ニューカッスル病疑い)の局地的な死亡事例であり、ヒトへの感染や重大な公衆衛生上の影響は確認されておらず、検査による確定診断も未実施のため。
triage.notes: ニューカッスル病は家禽感染症でヒトへの重大な健康被害は稀。ラボ確定診断がまだであり、地域住民からの懸念表明にとどまるため人間の感染症サーベイランスとしては優先度低い。

article.articleHeadline: Xử lý ổ dịch tả lợn châu Phi tại khu vực chăn nuôi lớn nhất phía Đông Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Containment of an African swine fever outbreak in the largest pig farming area in eastern Ho Chi Minh City.
article.articleSummary: 62 pigs were culled on August 22 in Tan Xuan hamlet, Xuan Son commune, eastern Ho Chi Minh City’s largest pig-farming area, as part of containment of an African swine fever outbreak. Laboratory confirmation by the Central Diagnostic and Testing Center for Veterinary Medicine II detected African swine fever virus in samples. Since 2026, Xuân Sơn has recorded two ASF outbreaks. Officials warn that variable weather may favor disease spread and urge farmers to report fever, loss of appetite, hemorrhages, weakness, or unexplained deaths promptly, avoiding self-treatment, movement, or disposal of sick pigs. Emphasize biosecurity: rigorous cleaning and disinfection, controlled access, proper waste and carcass disposal, and avoiding sale or transport of pigs of unknown origin. African swine fever is highly contagious with no specific treatment, though a vaccine exists.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市東部最大の養豚地域でアフリカ豚熱の発生を封じ込め
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱は豚のみに感染するウイルス性疾患でヒトへの健康影響はなく、局地的な封じ込め対応（62頭の淘汰）が行われているため、公衆衛生上のシグナルとしての優先度は低い。
triage.notes: ヒトに感染しない動物疾患（アフリカ豚熱）であり、IHR(2005)上の公衆衛生イベントには該当しない。畜産・食料安全保障への影響として動物衛生当局が監視すべき事案だが、EBSの人感染症シグナルとしては見送り。当該農場では2026年に既に2度目の発生であり、地域的な養豚業への経済的影響は継続監視の価値あり。

article.articleHeadline: 中, 한 달 새 코로나 52만명 '폭발'...韓도 심상치 않다
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 cases surge by 520,000 in a month; Korea is not looking good either.
article.articleSummary: China reports 522,000 new COVID-19 cases in August, with 487 severe cases and 1 death; NB.1.8.1 Omicron lineage is dominant. Across 1,041 sentinel hospitals, influenza-like illness tests show COVID-19 positivity rising from 8.2% (late Jun) to 21.2% (month-end), with about one in five suspected patients testing positive. In South Korea, Week 33 respiratory-virus surveillance shows a 9.1% COVID-19 detection rate among samples from 106 facilities (Sept 9–15), up from 3.2% in Week 30 and 5.7% in Week 32, while tertiary-hospital admissions increased from 2 to 7. BA.3.2 is driving Korea’s outbreak, though NB.1.8.1 is also detected domestically. Taiwan reports temporary vaccine stockouts amid surge. The government secured 4.84 million COVID-19 vaccine doses; Moderna’s Spikebox prefilled-syringe variant-targeting vaccine gained MFDS approval on Aug 6. Health authorities urge proactive vaccine procurement and continued personal preventive measures due to vaccine lead times and ongoing transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 中国、1か月でコロナ感染52万人『急増』…韓国も深刻
triage.triage_reason: 中国・韓国・台湾で新型コロナ陽性率が急上昇し、政府・メディアの関心も高いため、WPROスクリーニング基準（流行しやすさ・長期曝露）に該当し社会的関心も高いことからフルRRAへの移行を検討。
triage.notes: 韓国・台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。季節性のCOVID-19流行波であり重症化率は低いが、拡大傾向と社会的関心の高さからPICKUPと判定。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A
Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: อินเดียยกระดับเฝ้าระวังไข้หวัด "เอช1เอ็น1" หลังนิวเดลีพบผู้ป่วยแล้ว 1,777 คน
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India raises H1N1 influenza surveillance after New Delhi reports 1,777 cases.
article.articleSummary: As of August 23, 2026, India’s Health Ministry raised H1N1 influenza surveillance after New Delhi reported at least 1,777 H1N1 infections since the start of 2026. The ministry urged citizens to monitor for influenza A(H1N1) symptoms and seek prompt medical care if symptoms persist. Common signs include fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, and fatigue; some patients may experience lethargy, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, joint or muscle pain, and diarrhea. In New Delhi, the municipal authority instructed hospitals to heighten readiness with beds, ICU capacity, and essential supplies to handle a potential surge. Background: Influenza viruses can reassort genetically among human, swine, and other animal strains. The 2009 pandemic H1N1 virus carried genetic components from swine influenza and humans, leading to initial “swine flu” terms; the WHO/health agencies now refer to it as influenza A(H1N1) that circulates seasonally.

triage.headline_ja: インド、ニューデリーでH1N1インフルエンザ患者1,777人確認後、監視体制を強化
triage.triage_reason: ニューデリーでのH1N1感染者急増により、インド保健省が監視体制と病院の受け入れ体制強化を指示しており、重症度・拡大継続性・流行しやすさの観点から複数のWPRO基準に該当する。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)の国内流行であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候は記事上確認できない。ただし患者数の急増と病院の受け入れ体制強化指示から、フルリスク評価による経過確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: A double burden for women in dengue season
article.articleSummary: India faces a double burden of dengue and malaria on women during the monsoon season. Nearly 300,000 dengue cases were reported last year, with malaria still entrenched in the poorest districts. Women provide informal care in up to 83% of malaria cases and spend roughly four times more caregiving days than men. About 70% of community health workers are women, delivering care at personal risk and managing household mosquito control, yet their labor is rarely acknowledged or paid adequately. Dengue during pregnancy triples maternal mortality, and malaria raises pregnancy risks; women bear a higher burden of vector-borne diseases, with higher DALYs. Close to two-thirds of India’s female agricultural workers face heightened mosquito exposure simply by going to work. The first dengue vaccine approval is framed as reducing caregiving burdens and income losses, and policy should couple vaccination with strengthened vector control and gender-centered public health action.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱シーズンにおける女性への二重負担
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はインドにおけるデング熱・マラリアの女性への社会的負担に関する意見記事であり、新規の異常な感染症発生や急性のアウトブレイクを報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は意見・政策提言記事であり、デング熱・マラリアの流行地域における既知の疾病負担（特に女性への影響）を論じたものであり、新規の公衆衛生イベントではないためDISMISSと判定。

article.articleHeadline: DOH readies hospitals for leptospirosis surge after floods
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis preparedness in the Philippines amid floods. The Department of Health (DOH) activated a Leptospirosis Express Lane to speed treatment and mounted rapid diagnostic tests, antibiotics, and hemodialysis capacity at San Lazaro Hospital for moderate-to-severe cases. National readiness is in place, with DOH hospitals urged to stay prepared for a potential surge. San Lazaro Hospital has 50 active leptospirosis cases and two deaths amid flooding. From 4 January to mid-August 2026, 3,760 cases were recorded nationwide, with officials watching a recent uptick in admissions after heavy rains from the southwest monsoon. Floodwaters may be contaminated with rat urine and other infected animals, increasing exposure risk. Exposed individuals should seek medical advice within 24–48 hours to determine if prophylaxis is needed. More than 3.1 million doxycycline capsules have been prepositioned in regional facilities for prophylaxis when appropriate.

triage.headline_ja: DOH、洪水後のレプトスピラ症急増に備え病院を準備
triage.triage_reason: フィリピンで洪水後の季節性レプトスピラ症増加が報告されているが、既知の季節性疾患であり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。国内対応は進んでいるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 洪水後の季節性レプトスピラ症の増加であり、DOHが国内体制（迅速診断・抗菌薬・血液透析・予防投薬）を整備済み。全国で3,760例、San Lazaro病院で50例・死亡2例と報告されているが、例年の洪水関連流行パターンの範囲内とみられる。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Virus Mutating, Turning More Infectious: Dr Randeep Guleria On Swine Flu Case Surge In Delhi-NCR
article.articleSummary: H1N1 influenza is driving a Delhi-NCR surge, with 1,777 confirmed H1N1 cases this year—about sevenfold higher than the same period last year. The virus appears to be undergoing antigenic drift, making it more infectious and partially evading immunity from prior infections or vaccination. Monsoon humidity is aiding viral survival in the air, contributing to transmission. Clinically, many patients experience breathing difficulty and pneumonia, with some requiring hospitalization; older adults and those with comorbidities are at higher risk of severe illness. Common symptoms include fever, cough, body aches, sore throat, runny nose, and sometimes stomach upset or diarrhea; warning signs of deterioration include chest pain or tightness, breathlessness, a worsening cough with sputum, and high fever persisting 4–5 days. Household transmission is common, as one case can lead to others; officials emphasize precautions and note cases may decline as monsoon wanes.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1ウイルスが変異し感染力が増加：デリー首都圏で豚インフルエンザ症例急増についてランディープ・グレリア博士が指摘
triage.triage_reason: デリー首都圏でH1N1確定症例が前年比約7倍に急増し、抗原ドリフトによる感染力増加・免疫回避が疑われている点は異常かつ公衆衛生上の懸念があり、肺炎・入院例も報告されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 抗原ドリフトによる感染性増加の主張は専門家個人の見解であり、遺伝子解析等の公式確認情報は記事中に無い。続報でウイルス学的エビデンスの有無を確認する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie d'Ebola progresse de " façon exponentielle "
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is progressing exponentially.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is progressing exponentially, according to UN Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis from Bunia, the outbreak’s epicenter. The Bundibugyo-strain Ebola virus outbreak is accelerating faster than the response across the region. As of August 19, 2026, the epidemic has 5,290 confirmed cases, 2,516 deaths, and 1,152 recoveries, for a case-fatality rate of about 47.6%. The outbreak spans 56 health zones across six provinces and now covers an area larger than France. Deaths are mounting daily, with half occurring in the last 20 days. This is the largest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history, with authorities and the UN warning that transmission is expanding more rapidly than containment efforts, underscoring the urgent need for intensified control measures.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行は「指数関数的に」拡大している
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最大規模のエボラ流行で致死率約47.6%、6州56保健地区に拡大し封じ込めが追いついていないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 国連エボラ調整官が発言。史上最大規模の流行で、フランス国土より広い地域に拡大しているとの記述はDRCの流行規模を示す比喩であり、フランスは発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: RD Congo : une épidémie très meurtrière d'Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: A Very Deadly Ebola Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, now in its third month, has caused over 2,500 deaths and about 5,300 infections. The World Health Organization delivered more than 16,000 vaccines to Kinshasa for use against the Zaire ebolavirus strain; effectiveness against Bundibugyo is uncertain. Authorities plan to deploy the RVV vaccine, widely used during the 2018–2020 outbreak. To curb transmission, several towns, including Goma, have banned large gatherings, impacting local commerce. Frontline health workers face hostility from segments of the population, hindering aid delivery. UN agencies report insufficient response capacity. The affected area already exceeds the size of France, with officials fearing possible spread to the Central African Republic as concerns persist about containment. As of 23 August 2026, the outbreak stands as the country’s deadliest on record.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：非常に致死率の高いエボラ出血熱の流行
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱によりDRCで2,500人以上が死亡し、同国史上最悪の流行となっており、国際的拡大（中央アフリカ共和国への波及懸念）や渡航・集会制限も生じているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 中央アフリカ共和国への拡大懸念は記載されているが、実際の発生確認はDRCのみ。フランスは疾患発生国ではなく報道元のため除外。ワクチン効果不確実性やヘルスワーカーへの敵意など対応能力に懸念あり。

article.articleHeadline: NKTI reaches full bed capacity amid leptospirosis surge
article.articleSummary: As of Aug. 23, 2026, the National Kidney and Transplant Institute (NKTI) in the Philippines is at full bed capacity amid a surge in leptospirosis. Walk-in admissions to the emergency room are limited until further notice, with urgent and critical patients prioritized. Those seeking elective or non-emergency admissions should coordinate with attending physicians and consider other facilities with available beds to avoid prolonged waiting times. NKTI notes the emergency department is experiencing high patient volume. Earlier, heavy rains from the southwest monsoon (Habagat) triggered flooding across areas of the country.

triage.headline_ja: レプトスピラ症急増によりNKTIが病床数の上限に達する
triage.triage_reason: フィリピンでレプトスピラ症患者の急増により主要病院が満床となり、緊急以外の受け入れを制限するなど医療体制への深刻な影響が見られるため。
triage.notes: モンスーン季の洪水に伴う季節性のレプトスピラ症急増であり、異常性は低いが、医療機関の受け入れ能力逼迫という重大な公衆衛生影響が確認されている。続報でヒト-ヒト感染の可能性や国際的支援の必要性を確認する必要がある。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: Two Respiratory Illnesses, Different Realities: H1N1 Vs Covid - Difference Explained
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, H1N1 is a strain of influenza A causing seasonal flu, while Covid-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2. Both transmit via airborne particles and share fever, cough, fatigue, headaches, sore throat and body aches; Covid-19 may also cause loss or changes in taste and smell. Differences lie in onset and variability: influenza symptoms typically appear suddenly, while Covid-19 symptoms vary by person; severity depends on age, underlying conditions, and immune status. Testing helps distinguish infections when symptoms overlap; a clinician can guide testing based on symptoms, exposure, and local circulation of respiratory viruses. Recognize symptoms, take precautions, and seek medical advice if symptoms worsen to reduce complications and transmission. View H1N1 and Covid-19 as distinct infections with similar presentations, not interchangeable.

triage.headline_ja: 2つの呼吸器疾患、異なる実態:H1N1とCovidの違いを解説
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はH1N1とCOVID-19の症状の違いを解説する一般啓発記事であり、具体的な発生事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事は疾患の一般的な比較・啓発内容であり、インドにおける具体的な症例数や流行状況の記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: تفشٍ عالمي للحصبة.. ملايين الإصابات المتوقعة هذا العام... - الوكيل الإخباري
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Global measles outbreak... millions of infections expected this year.
article.articleSummary: Global measles outbreak accelerates in 2026, with an estimated 11 million infections, concentrated in Africa and Asia, and with hotspots in Europe and the Americas. The surge is largely attributed to falling vaccination rates, compounded by COVID-19-related delays in routine immunizations. Measles is highly contagious and can lead to serious complications, underscoring vaccination as the most effective prevention. Several countries have experienced wide outbreaks, including Yemen, Sudan, Somalia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, India, Bangladesh, and the United States, with warnings that transmission will continue unless immunization coverage rises.

triage.headline_ja: 世界的なはしか(麻疹)の流行拡大…今年は数百万人の感染が予想される
triage.triage_reason: 世界的な麻疹流行が加速し、深刻な合併症リスクと国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準を2つ以上満たすためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は複数国（イエメン、スーダン、ソマリア、バングラデシュ、米国など）を挙げた世界的な麻疹流行の概況記事。対象国リストに含まれるのはコンゴ民主共和国とインドのみ。ワクチン接種率低下とCOVID-19による定期接種の遅延が要因とされる。
