article.articleHeadline: Swine Flu Cases Delhi: Health Ministry Issues Fresh Advisory
article.articleSummary: Influenza A H1N1 drives a fresh public-health advisory as Delhi reports 1,777 H1N1 cases through August 20. The Health Ministry urges anyone with fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches or fatigue to seek medical care, highlighting a seasonal monsoon-linked rise in respiratory infections. While many infections are mild, older adults and people with preexisting conditions face higher risk and should obtain prompt medical assessment. Delhi hospitals report readiness with beds, doctors, medicines and equipment. The outbreak context extends beyond Delhi to Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai, with Kerala recording high influenza activity and deaths. NDTV notes evolving counts and underscores vaccination's role. Officials advise monitoring Health Ministry, state health departments and hospital updates as surveillance continues and numbers may change.

triage.headline_ja: デリーの豚インフルエンザ症例:保健省が新たな勧告を発表
triage.triage_reason: インドで季節性のH1N1インフルエンザが複数都市（デリー、ムンバイ、ベンガルール、チェンナイ、ケララ）に拡大し死亡例も報告されているが、既知の病原体で毎年恒例の季節性流行パターンであり、IHR基準の該当は乏しいため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)の毎年恒例の流行で、モンスーン期に伴う呼吸器感染症の増加。デリーで1,777例、ケララで死亡例あり。既知病原体であり異常性は低いが、症例数増加と複数州拡大のため続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: 剛果伊波拉疫情失控 Pope Leo XIV呼籲國際馳援 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo Ebola Outbreak Out of Control; Pope Leo XIV Appeals for International Aid - Minshi News Network
article.articleSummary: Out-of-control Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is described as the deadliest in history, with health officials warning exponential spread and thousands of lives lost. The hardest-hit areas are in northern and eastern DR Congo, where weak government capacity, severely limited healthcare infrastructure, and ongoing armed conflict hinder containment and response. Pope Leo XIV urges international aid and active local community cooperation to save lives and halt transmission. The report emphasizes urgency but does not provide exact case counts or laboratory confirmation details. The focus remains on the Congo outbreak and the need for sustained public health action from global partners and local authorities to curb transmission, amid a fragile regional security environment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・エボラ疫病が制御不能に、ローマ教皇レオ14世が国際支援を呼びかけ - 民視新聞網
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで「史上最悪」レベルで指数関数的に拡大していると報告され、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際支援の必要性が明確であるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事には具体的な症例数や検査確認の詳細が欠けているが、教皇による国際支援要請など社会的関心が非常に高い。武力紛争と脆弱な保健インフラが対応を困難にしている点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: Pope appeals for international aid for Ebola victims in DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Bundibugyo strain) with 5,300 confirmed cases and more than 2,500 deaths; World Health Organization declared the epidemic in May 2026, with cases also reported in Uganda. The DRC has received over 16,000 doses of Ervebo, though no approved treatment or vaccine exists for Bundibugyo. Spread hindered by armed conflict in key outbreak cities. Pope Leo XIV urged international aid and emphasized local-community involvement in prevention to save lives. Separately, in the Central African Republic, a mining accident at the Zamboyé open-pit gold mine on August 18 killed over 100 people; authorities said the site had been closed before the collapse, and prayers were offered for victims and mining safety.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱被害者への国際支援を訴え
triage.triage_reason: WHOが緊急事態を宣言したエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)のアウトブレイクで死者2,500人超、ウガンダへの拡大、承認された治療薬・ワクチンがない状況であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・中央アフリカ共和国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。中央アフリカ共和国の鉱山事故は感染症と無関係な別事案。

article.articleHeadline: המרוץ נגד האבולה: 70 אלף חיסונים נשלחים לקונגו
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The race against Ebola: 70,000 vaccines are being sent to Congo.
article.articleSummary: WHO and Africa CDC have allocated 70,000 Ervebo vaccine doses to the Democratic Republic of Congo to tackle a large Ebola outbreak driven by Bundibugyo virus. Ervebo is licensed for Ebola virus (Zaire ebolavirus); there is no licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo. Of the 70,000 doses, 20,000 will be used in a Phase 3 trial to assess whether Ervebo can protect against Bundibugyo, while 50,000 doses will go to frontline health workers. Early lab/animal data hint at possible cross-protection, but clinical evidence is lacking. As of August 18, 2026, Congo reported 5,208 confirmed cases and over 2,476 deaths (case fatality ~47.5%), across 56 health zones in Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Bas-Uélé, and Tshopo. The outbreak is among the largest ever; imported cases have occurred but there is no sustained transmission outside DRC. Domestic/regional risk is high; global risk remains low amid security and health-system challenges.

triage.headline_ja: エボラとの闘い:7万回分のワクチンがコンゴに送られる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大級規模のエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行が継続しており、致死率約47.5%、5,208症例超と深刻。IHR基準複数該当かつWHO/Africa CDCによる緊急ワクチン投入という国際的対応が進行中。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoウイルス株によるエボラ流行で、既存のErvebo（ザイール株用）ワクチンの交差防御効果を検証する第3相試験が進行中。輸入症例はあるがDRC域外での持続的伝播は確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Pápež Lev XIV. vyzval k pomoci Kongu v boji proti ebole
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pope Leo XIV urged Congo to help in the fight against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Pope Leo XIV urged international aid for the Democratic Republic of Congo to combat a spreading Ebola outbreak that has claimed many lives, emphasizing preventive actions that involve local communities. He also expressed solidarity with the Central African Republic’s mourning population after a mining collapse in Zamboyé and called for safety and rule-of-law enforcement in mining regions. The Pope marked the upcoming tenth anniversary of the August 24, 2016, central Italy earthquake that devastated Lazio, Umbria, and Marche, praying for the deceased, their families, and ongoing reconstruction. He closed by greeting Rome residents and pilgrims, including the Primatial Cathedral Choir from Gniezno (Poland), seminarians and leaders of the Pontifical North American College, and youths from Bormio and Valfurva, blessing all on Sunday.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇レオ14世、エボラと闘うコンゴへの支援を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で拡大中のエボラ出血熱流行に対し、教皇が国際的支援を呼びかけており、重症度・拡散リスクの観点からフルRRAでの確認が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: 本記事は教皇の呼びかけを報じる二次的な宗教・政治的コンテンツであり、疫学的な新規データ（症例数・致死率等）は含まれていない。コンゴのエボラ流行自体は既知の継続事案であるため、既存のRRA・モニタリング状況を確認の上で判断する必要がある。イタリア・ポーランド・中央アフリカ共和国の地名は地震十周年や鉱山事故など別事案に関連し、エボラとは無関係。

article.articleHeadline: El Papa pide la cooperación internacional para frenar el brote de ébola en Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope calls for international cooperation to curb the Ebola outbreak in Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of August 20, 2026, Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reached 5,375 confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths, for a case fatality rate of 47.6%. The current outbreak is the second deadliest globally and the most infections recorded in the country. Of those affected, 737 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, and 1,167 have recovered. Contact tracing stands at 85.5%, surpassing the 85% target. Pope Leo XIV called for an international response that also involves local communities in preventive efforts to save lives, stated during the Sunday Angelus. Data reflect the government bulletin through August 20, highlighting the ongoing need for action as the outbreak persists.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴのエボラ流行阻止に向けた国際協力を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で5,375人の確定症例、致死率47.6%という大規模なエボラ流行が継続しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、教皇の呼びかけにより社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 致死率47.6%と非常に高く、症例数・死亡者数ともに過去最大級の規模。教皇による国際協力の呼びかけは国際的関心の高さを示す。フルRRAでの詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Rd Congo, il Papa: la comunità internazionale aiuti a salvare vite umane
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo, the Pope: the international community should help save human lives.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused over 2,500 deaths and more than 5,300 cases, with a current case fatality rate around 47.6%. This ongoing outbreak is the second deadliest in DRC history, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that killed about 11,000 and sickened 28,000. Pope Francis, speaking after the Angelus, urged a united international response and stressed the importance of involving local communities in prevention to save lives. The remarks underscore the continued need for global solidarity to curb transmission and protect affected populations as of 23 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、教皇：国際社会は人命救助に協力すべき
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は5,300症例・2,500人以上の死亡、致死率47.6%と深刻で、史上2番目に致命的な流行とされ、国際社会への支援要請もなされている。
triage.notes: 発生地域にCentral African RepublicとAngolaが含まれているが、記事本文ではDRCの流行のみが具体的に言及されており、他国での発生については記載がないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Papež poziva domačo in mednarodno skupnost pri zajezitvi ebole v Demokratični republiki Kongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope calls on the domestic and international community to contain Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: On 23 August 2026, the Pope urged the domestic and international community to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, emphasizing local community involvement in prevention to save lives. The address highlights the ongoing epidemic in DRC and the need for a coordinated response. In a separate note of solidarity, the Pope expressed closeness to the people of the Central African Republic, who mourn a mine collapse in Zamboyéju, urging safety and rule of law in mining areas. He also marked the 10th anniversary of the central Italy earthquake affecting Lazio, Umbria, and Marche, praying for the deceased, their families, and ongoing rebuilding efforts. The article ties spiritual leadership to public health and disaster aid, without providing detailed outbreak metrics.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行封じ込めに向け国内外の共同体に呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ出血熱流行に関し、教皇が国際社会に支援を呼びかけている。エボラは重症度が高く国際的懸念のある疾患であり、フルリスク評価による現状確認が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は教皇の呼びかけを中心とした内容で、具体的な症例数・死亡者数等の疫学的詳細は含まれていない。DRCで進行中のエボラ流行の現状について別途情報源での確認が必要。中央アフリカ共和国の鉱山事故やイタリア地震の言及は本イベントとは無関係。

article.articleHeadline: Youth caravan steps up Ebola awareness amid attacks on response teams
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), centered in Beni and spanning Ituri and North Kivu, with Mongbwalu and Rwampara hotspots. Burial teams have been attacked and treatment centers burned as response efforts contend with violence and insecurity fueled by rumors. The current outbreak has become the second deadliest in history since it was declared earlier this year and is on track to be the largest, spreading several times faster than the 2014 West Africa epidemic. Beni was the epicenter of the 2018–2020 outbreak and is again affected. A youth caravan organized by local youths with Congolese NGOs and the World Health Organization rode through Beni to raise awareness and boost youth involvement. Officials emphasize community engagement to counter hostility toward health workers and urge stronger government support despite funds unlocked.

triage.headline_ja: 対応チームへの攻撃が続く中、若者キャラバンがエボラ啓発活動を強化
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上2番目に死亡者数の多いエボラ流行が拡大中で、2014年西アフリカ流行より速いペースで感染が広がっており、公衆衛生上重大かつ国際的拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwanda・Angolaが含まれているが、記事本文はDRC（Beni、Ituri、North Kivu）における流行に焦点を当てており、両国での発生は言及されていないため除外した。治安悪化・医療従事者への攻撃により対応が困難化しており、外部支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Bali reassures foreign tourists concerning Zika
article.articleSummary: On 23 August 2026, Bali Tourism Office reassured international travelers after a US health advisory on Zika, affirming Bali as a safe and comfortable destination. Denpasar-based officials, led by Head I Wayan Sumarajaya, said the office is coordinating with the Bali Provincial Health Office. Authorities have officially confirmed that no Zika infections have been detected or reported anywhere in Bali to date. Despite this, tourists and industry stakeholders should implement preventive measures against mosquito-borne diseases due to Bali’s tropical climate, similar to dengue fever precautions, and avoid mosquito bites. The Bali Tourism Office urged all tourism service providers to maintain high health standards, cleanliness, and guest comfort to support safe travel.

triage.headline_ja: バリ、ジカ熱に関して外国人観光客に安全性を保証
triage.triage_reason: 米国の注意喚起を受けた観光局の安全宣言であり、バリでのジカ熱感染は確認されていない。実際の症例発生がないため公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はジカ熱感染例がないことの確認と観光業界向けの予防喚起であり、米国の渡航注意情報への対応記事。実際の症例報告なし。

article.articleHeadline: Papa Leão XIV pede mais esforços internacionais para conter Ebola na RD Congo | Jovem Pan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pope Leo XIV Calls for Greater International Efforts to Contain Ebola in the DRC | Jovem Pan.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-23, Pope Leo XIV called for intensified international efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, urging involvement of local communities in the response. The appeal targets northern and eastern DRC regions where state presence is limited, health infrastructure is weak, and armed groups operate, with authorities noting rapid viral spread. Ebola, caused by a virus, triggers fever, bleeding and other severe symptoms and spreads via contact with blood and other bodily fluids. The pope highlighted that the disease has already caused thousands of deaths in Ebola epidemics historically. He also expressed solidarity for victims of a gold-mine landslide in the Central African Republic near the Cameroonian border, where dozens died and many remain missing. Prayers were also offered for the 10th anniversary of the Central Italy earthquake around Amatrice.

triage.headline_ja: レオ14世教皇、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ熱封じ込めへの国際的な取り組み強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国での急速なエボラウイルス拡大が当局により指摘され、国際的な支援要請が教皇からもなされていることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事は主にコンゴ民主共和国北部・東部でのエボラ拡大について報じており、中央アフリカ共和国の金鉱山地滑りやイタリア中部地震への言及はエボラとは無関係の別トピックのため、対象国から除外した。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases rise: ICMR says no new strain but high-risk groups need caution
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, India reports ongoing circulation of Influenza A (H1N1) pdm09 viruses, not a new strain. The circulating lineage is A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like, clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, circulating since 2025. No novel strain identified, and current strains are well matched to Northern Hemisphere vaccine strains. H1N1 is largely self-limiting; common symptoms include fever, cough, headache and body ache. High-risk groups—young children, the elderly, and those with underlying conditions—may have higher complication risk. Delhi has issued a public health advisory for respiratory hygiene and masks in crowded places, with medical attention urged for flu-like symptoms. Delhi reports over 1,777 H1N1 cases this year, including 114 new cases on Thursday, and total Influenza-A cases surpassing 2,300. Surveillance continues with 35 hospitals under special surveillance; AIIMS and NCDC testing labs designated.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1感染者増加：ICMRは新規株ではないとしつつ、高リスク群への注意を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1症例が増加しているが、ICMRは新規株ではなく季節性インフルエンザの通常の流行と説明しており、IHR基準には該当しない。地域的な監視体制強化はあるが、国際的関心・拡大リスクは低い。
triage.notes: MissouriはウイルスのクレードA/Missouri/11/2025株名に由来する地名であり、実際の発生地域ではないため除外。United Statesも同様の理由で除外。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: Delhi sees rise in H1N1 cases as government issues alert. Know symptoms, precautions and how does it spread
article.articleSummary: Delhi records a sharp rise in H1N1 infections, prompting a public health advisory. The city has logged more than 1,777 H1N1 cases this year, including 114 new infections reported on Thursday, and over 2,300 Influenza-A cases, prompting strengthened preparedness. H1N1 spreads mainly through respiratory droplets and can also spread via contaminated surfaces. Residents are urged to wear masks in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces, wash hands regularly, cover coughs or sneezes, and maintain distance from people with respiratory symptoms. Additional precautions include avoiding touching eyes, nose or mouth with unwashed hands, not spitting in public, and seeking medical attention if symptoms are severe or persistent, especially with breathing difficulty or chest pain. H1N1 affects all ages but poses greater risk of severe illness for children and those with underlying conditions.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染者が増加、政府が警戒を発令 症状・予防法・受診の目安について
triage.triage_reason: デリーでのH1N1感染者増加を受け政府が注意喚起を出しているが、季節性インフルエンザの範囲内であり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いと判断されるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: H1N1・インフルエンザAの症例数増加はデリー地域内の季節性流行として報告されており、重症度や死亡者数についての具体的記載はない。政府による予防啓発が中心で、外部支援の必要性は示唆されていない。

article.articleHeadline: O apelo de Leão XIV: trabalhar na prevenção do Ebola para salvar vidas na RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Appeal of Leo XIV: Working on Ebola Prevention to Save Lives in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 2,500 people in three months, with no vaccines or specific treatments available. The Bundibugyo strain drives the outbreak, described as the deadliest in the country’s history. The Pope Leo XIV, delivering a Sunday Angelus from St. Peter’s Square, appealed for an international response to save many lives. UN briefings on 21 August note exponential growth and rapid cross-border movement that hinder surveillance, care, and transmission control amid armed conflict and population displacement. A Nature Microbiology study reports persistence of the Ebola virus in the central nervous system after the acute phase, complicating recovery. The article underscores urgent global action as health systems remain fragile and access is limited in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: レオ14世の訴え：コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行を防ぐために命を救う努力を
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準を複数満たし（深刻な公衆衛生影響・異常性・国際的拡大リスク）、コンゴ史上最悪とされるエボラ流行で国際的関心・支援要請も高いためフルリスク評価に進むべき。
triage.notes: 発生地域にVatican Cityが含まれるが、これは教皇の発言拠点であり実際の発生国はDRCのみ。3ヶ月で2500人以上死亡、ブンディブギョ株による同国史上最悪の流行とされ、武力紛争・住民移動により対策が困難な状況。

article.articleHeadline: El Papa pide a la comunidad internacional que responda al brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope appeals to the international community to respond to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Pope appeals for international action to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. On the 100th day since the outbreak declaration, the epidemic has claimed more than 2,500 lives in the DRC, amid ongoing armed conflict. The Pontiff urged a coordinated global response that also engages local communities in prevention to save lives. The report centers on the Ebola crisis and the need for robust public health measures, timely support, and international solidarity. No laboratory-confirmed details, transmission specifics, or symptom descriptions are provided beyond the stated mortality toll.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクへの国際社会の対応を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱で死者2,500人超という深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、武力紛争下での対応の困難さ、教皇による国際支援要請など社会的関心も高いため、フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は死者数（2,500人超）と発生100日目という節目、武力紛争の影響、国際支援の必要性に焦点を当てているが、検査確定症例数や感染経路等の疫学的詳細は記載なし。既存の大規模アウトブレイクの継続報道であるため、既知情報との重複確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: We Must Meet the Challenge and Stop Ebola - WHO and Africa CDC
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by a Bundibugyo strain, is 100 days since its declaration; border closures have not occurred. The piece emphasizes that global response is hampered by a lack of international interest and support, a major obstacle to protecting local communities and reducing global health risk. Historical context notes the West Africa epidemic (2014–2016) that killed about 12,000 and led to the withdrawal of aid to Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia, leaving health workers poorly supplied. Ebola transmission requires close contact with a clearly ill person, unlike hantavirus or measles. Heads of WHO and Africa CDC urge renewed world commitment, stating the epidemic can be controlled with resolve. No specific case/death counts are provided; the focus is on political will, resources, and sustained public health measures to stop transmission.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの課題に立ち向かい阻止せねばならない ― WHOとアフリカCDC
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で継続中のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）流行が宣言から100日を迎え、国際的な関心・支援不足が指摘されており、IHR基準複数該当かつWHO/Africa CDCが懸念を表明している。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国東部での現行エボラ流行（ブンディブギョ株）が主題。シエラレオネ・アンゴラ・リベリア・ギニアは2014-2016年西アフリカ流行の歴史的文脈として言及されているのみで、現行の発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した。具体的な症例数・死亡者数は記事に記載なし。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: No cause for panic over H1N1; current strains in circulation since 2025, says ICMR
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, India reports no new Influenza A (H1N1) strain; circulating H1N1 pdm09 viruses resemble A/Missouri/11/2025, in clade 6B.1A.5a2a and subclade D.3.1.1, with circulation ongoing since 2025. The strains are well matched to Northern Hemisphere vaccine strains. Seasonal influenza, including H1N1, remains mostly self-limiting; common symptoms include fever, cough, headache and body aches, with most individuals recovering with rest and appropriate care. Young children, elderly people, and those with underlying conditions are at greater risk of complications. Ongoing surveillance and public health measures are in place. In Delhi, a health-review meeting chaired by Union Health Minister JP Nadda reviewed preparedness for seasonal and vector-borne diseases; Delhi officials state hospitals are prepared, with no shortages of beds, medicines or essential equipment, ensuring timely diagnosis and treatment.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1について懸念不要、現在流通している株は2025年から確認されているとICMRが発表
triage.triage_reason: インドの保健当局が新規株ではなく既存の季節性H1N1株であることを確認し、ワクチンとも適合しており、パニックの必要はないと公式に否定している内容であり、異常性・重篤性・国際的拡大リスクはいずれも認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)が2025年から継続して流行している既知株であり、ワクチン株と一致し、通常の自己限定的な疾患であることを政府機関が説明する内容。デリーでの保健準備会議も通常の季節性対策の一環であり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Pope calls for more efforts to stop Ebola in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, Ebola virus outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo are spreading exponentially, described by health officials as the deadliest in the DRC's history and having already killed thousands. The epidemic affects northern and eastern regions where state presence is weak and health infrastructure is largely lacking, with armed groups contributing to the crisis. Pope Leo XIV urged the international community to bolster containment efforts and to involve local communities in lifesaving actions. The pope's appeal signals a global responsibility to support vaccination, surveillance, isolation, and care in DR Congo, though the report provides no exact case counts, laboratory confirmation details, or identified infection sources. The call focuses on accelerating international aid to curb the outbreak and save lives in affected areas.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行阻止へさらなる努力を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪とされるエボラ流行が指数関数的に拡大し、既に多数の死者が出ているとされ、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進める。
triage.notes: 記事には正確な症例数、検査確認情報、感染源の特定はなく、教皇の呼びかけを中心とした報道。武装勢力の存在や医療インフラの脆弱性が流行拡大の一因とされている。続報でWHO等の公式データ確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 剛果伊波拉疫情奪2500命　教宗Leo呼籲國際社會馳援 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo claims 2,500 lives; Pope Leo urges the international community to rush to aid - Ming Shih News Network
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the deadliest in the country’s history, with more than 2,500 lives lost and case numbers climbing across large areas as of late July 2026. United Nations officials noted the rapid spread and record-high infections and deaths within Congo. Reuters reports the outbreak remains ongoing, demanding intensified global support and coordinated public health action to save lives.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mask-wearing days are back; Swine flu alert issued in Delhi; Who is at greater risk? What antibiotics should you take?
article.articleSummary: Delhi, India, issues an H1N1 swine-flu alert with public health guidelines. As of 23 August 2026, the city has recorded 1,777 H1N1 infections this year and over 2,600 total influenza cases, with 114 new infections reported on Thursday. Higher risk groups include the elderly, pregnant women, and people with heart or lung disease or weakened immunity. Dr. Arjun Khanna of Amrita Hospital warns influenza can lead to pneumonia, hypoxemia, or respiratory failure in vulnerable individuals. Key measures: mask in crowded places, frequent handwashing, cover coughs and sneezes, avoid touching the face, practice distancing from the ill, stay hydrated, and stay home when sick. Antibiotics do not cure influenza; they help only with secondary bacterial infections. Vaccination reduces infection risk by about 30% and lowers hospitalization if infected, per 2025–26 data. WHO notes about 1 billion global influenza cases annually.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Papa pede resposta internacional para travar epidemia na RDCongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Pope calls for an international response to halt the Ebola epidemic in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Ebola outbreak has reached 5,375 confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths, with a case fatality rate of 47.6% as of data through August 20. Six provinces are affected: Ituri (epicenter), North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, and South Kivu. About 737 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, and 1,167 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 85.5%, above the 85% target. Vaccination efforts include Ervebo (for Zaire ebolavirus) showing potential efficacy against Bundibugyo in animal studies, and two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines in Phase 1 trials that have shown safety. The outbreak is the fastest-growing since the WHO’s declaration and could reach the scale of the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (approximately 11,000 deaths). Ebola transmits via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding. The Pope urged an international response that includes local communities in prevention.

article.articleHeadline: India News | No Cause for Panic over H1N1; Current Strains in Circulation Since 2025, Says ICMR
article.articleSummary: Influenza A (H1N1) in India: ICMR states no new strain detected; circulating H1N1 pdm09 viruses match A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like strain, clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, in circulation since 2025. Viruses well matched to Northern Hemisphere vaccine strains. No cause for panic; seasonal influenza is mostly self-limiting. Common symptoms include fever, cough, headache, and body aches; most recover with rest and appropriate care. Higher risk for young children, elderly, and those with underlying conditions, who should seek medical advice if symptoms persist. Ongoing surveillance and public health measures are being undertaken. In Delhi, a health review meeting confirmed preparedness: no shortage of beds, medicines, or essential equipment; hospital readiness and timely diagnosis and treatment for patients. Government data cited indicate 2,392 influenza-A cases in 2026 up to August 21, with 1,777 confirmed as H1N1; this is about eight times higher than the 229 H1N1 cases recorded by the same date last year. Preventive guidance includes rest, hydration, avoiding crowded places, and seeking medical care for high fever, breathing difficulties, or chest pain, noting the survey is not an official tally.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In DR Congo, urged to intensify the fight against the Ebola outbreak two to threefold
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, requires a two- to threefold expansion of response measures, per a column in Al Jazeera English. As of 21 August, authorities reported 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths across 56 health zones. The current outbreak is the second-largest on record and is spreading faster than prior major episodes. Ongoing conflict and instability have weakened health systems, and more than a million people have been displaced. Healthcare workers remain at high risk: by 20 August, 158 staff were infected and 45 had died. Calls emphasize PPE, training, clean water, sanitation, timely salaries, psychosocial support, rapid diagnostics, and quality care. The response involves DRC authorities, local experts, WHO, Africa CDC, and partners, expanding surveillance, laboratories, treatment centers, and supply chains. Key measures include early detection, contact tracing, safe treatment, and dignified burials; cross-border information sharing and mobility monitoring are prioritized over travel restrictions.

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai's Stray Dogs To Get QR-Enabled Collars: BMC Plans To Eliminate Rabies By 2030
article.articleSummary: Rabies elimination drive in Mumbai: BMC introduces QR-enabled reflective collars for stray dogs to replace fading ink marks, linking each dog to a digital record of rabies vaccination and sterilisation status, health data, and follow-up needs. The system, developed with Ridlan AI Foundation's PawFriend.in, aims to help BMC, animal welfare groups, and citizens identify dogs already vaccinated or sterilised and flag those requiring intervention, thereby monitoring vaccination and sterilisation coverage and reducing duplication. Current practice uses coloured ink and temporary markings that fade over time. The durable collars provide authorized access to the registry and enable tracking of progress toward the city’s objective of eliminating rabies by 2030, in line with Supreme Court directions. BMC emphasizes technology-driven, transparent, and scientifically managed stray dog population management and rabies prevention to contribute to national dog-mediated rabies elimination.

article.articleHeadline: 'No Need To Panic, Virus Self-Limiting': ICMR Says Swine Flu Strain Not New As Cases Rise In Delhi; Check Prevention Tips
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, ICMR says no new influenza A(H1N1) strain identified in India; circulating viruses resemble A/Missouri/11/2025 and have circulated since 2025. Most infections are self-limiting with fever, cough, headache and body aches. Delhi has seen a surge in H1N1 cases, with over 1,700 infections recorded so far. Transmission is via respiratory droplets; the virus can spread through touching contaminated surfaces and can survive 24–48 hours on hard surfaces. Infectiousness begins about one day before symptoms and lasts about five to seven days after onset. Monsoon conditions may contribute to the seasonal rise. Prevention includes frequent handwashing, covering coughs/sneezes, avoiding close contact with the ill, and staying home when symptomatic. Laboratory confirmation aligns with A/Missouri/11/2025; no evidence of a new strain. Doctors should be consulted if symptoms persist or worsen; authorities continue monitoring.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Expands as Frontline Workers Go Unpaid
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri region, driven by Bundibugyo virus, marks the 17th outbreak in the country. As of 2026-08-23, across 56 health zones there are over 5,000 confirmed cases and more than 2,500 deaths. WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, with Africa CDC also declaring a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. Frontline workers in Bunia face unpaid wages amid insecurity and mass displacement, highlighting funding gaps that threaten response effectiveness. Community-led responses are advancing early detection and safe burial practices, though tensions between trust and official measures complicate coordination. Without rapid funding and security improvements, the outbreak could become the largest on record, underscoring the need to scale up surveillance, PPE, staffing, and protections for health workers.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why are swine flu cases increasing in Delhi-NCR? How dangerous is H1N1? Symptoms explained by Dr. Randeep Guleria.
article.articleSummary: Delhi-NCR reports 1,777 lab-confirmed H1N1 (swine flu) cases this season, indicating a rising outbreak. Dr. Randeep Guleria attributes the surge to antigenic drift—small, time-dependent changes in the virus that can weaken prior immunity from infection or vaccination—though mutation is a normal process and panic is unwarranted. Monsoon-related shifts in temperature and humidity may promote respiratory illnesses, with some patients developing breathlessness or pneumonia. Typical H1N1 symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, body pains, and fatigue; warning signs of severe disease include shortness of breath, chest pain or heaviness, persistent productive cough, or fever lasting multiple days. Preventive measures emphasize masking in crowded places, hand hygiene, covering coughs, avoiding sick children in school, and vaccination for seniors and those with diabetes or hypertension to reduce risk of severe illness and hospitalization.

triage.headline_ja: デリー・NCRでスワインフル(H1N1)症例が増加している理由とは？H1N1の危険性は？ランディープ・グレリア医師が症状を解説

article.articleHeadline: البابا يدعو لتكثيف جهود احتواء تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديموقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope urges intensified efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-23, Pope Lawon XIV urged intensified international help to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Speaking after the Angelus at St. Peter’s Square, he prayed for the DRC and called on the international community and local communities to take stronger preventive actions to save lives. The outbreak is described as the deadliest in the DRC’s history, having claimed thousands of lives and spreading through northern and eastern regions, in areas with weak health infrastructure and ongoing armed conflict. The pope stressed solidarity with those affected and linked the appeal to broader humanitarian concerns in Africa. The article underscores the urgency of intensified efforts to halt transmission and protect vulnerable populations amid a major Ebola crisis in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行封じ込めへの取り組み強化を呼びかけ

article.articleHeadline: नया स्ट्रेन या पुराना वायरस और कितना खतरा? H1N1 पर ICMR ने दिया जवाब
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New strain or old virus, and how dangerous is it? ICMR gives the answer on H1N1.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A (H1N1) pdm09 virus circulating in India is A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like, linked to clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, in circulation since 2025. No new strain detected; current strains align with Northern Hemisphere seasonal vaccine strains for the season. Seasonal influenza including H1N1 is largely self-limiting. Common symptoms include fever, cough, headache, and body pains; most people recover with rest in about 3–4 days. High-risk groups include young children, the elderly, and those with underlying conditions, who may develop complications. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek medical advice promptly. Ongoing surveillance and public health measures are in place in India. Not every fever or cough is H1N1, so panic is unnecessary.

triage.headline_ja: 新しい株か、既存のウイルスか？その危険性は？H1N1についてICMRが回答
triage.triage_reason: ICMRが新規変異株ではなく既知の季節性インフルエンザ株であることを公式に確認し、自己限定的な疾患と説明しているため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はICMR（インド医学研究評議会）が新規株の噂を否定し、季節性インフルエンザとして通常の対応で十分と説明する内容。パニックを鎮める趣旨の広報記事であり、公衆衛生上の新たな脅威を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: León XIV expresó su preocupación por el ébola y las tragedias que golpean África
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Leon XIV expressed his concern about Ebola and the tragedies that strike Africa.
article.articleSummary: After reciting the Angelus in St. Peter's Square, Pope Leo XIV expressed concern about the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, urging a stronger international response and greater local-community involvement in prevention and health care to save lives. He extended solidarity to those affected by the mining collapse in the Central African Republic at Zamboyé on August 18, noting more than 100 fatalities and calling for improved mining safety and enforcement. He also marked the ten-year anniversary of the August 24, 2016 earthquake in central Italy—affecting Lazio, Umbria, and Marche—with 299 deaths, about 400 injuries, and over 40,000 displaced, praying for victims and reconstruction. The Angelus address tied these tragedies to calls for faith, solidarity, and responsible governance.

triage.headline_ja: レオ14世、エボラとアフリカを襲う悲劇への懸念を表明
triage.triage_reason: エボラ自体は重大疾患だが、本記事は教皇による懸念表明であり、DRCでの具体的な症例数・発生状況等の新規疫学情報を含まないため、続報の確認が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は教皇レオ14世によるDRCエボラ流行への懸念表明・国際支援要請に関するもので、具体的な症例数や発生地詳細等の新規情報は含まれていない。中央アフリカ共和国の鉱山事故とイタリア地震への言及は感染症とは無関係で対象国リストにも該当しないため除外。DRCのエボラ流行状況については既存の継続モニタリング対象と考えられ、本記事単独では新規シグナルとしての価値は限定的。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola u DR Kongu. Papa: Neka međunarodna zajednica pomogne spasiti živote
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DR Congo. Pope: Let the international community help save lives.
article.articleSummary: as of 23 August 2026: The Pope urged international support to curb Ebola spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where deaths exceed 2,500 and confirmed cases exceed 5,300, with a 47.6% case-fatality rate. The outbreak is the second-deadliest in DRC history, after 2014–2016 West Africa. In his Angelus address, he called for coordinated prevention by international and local communities to save lives. The Pope also noted a gold mine collapse in Zamboyeu, Central African Republic, on 18 August, killing over 100 and prompting government closure for safety/regulatory shortcomings. He referenced the 24 August 2016 Central Italy earthquake (Lazio, Marche, Umbria, Abruzzo), which left 299 dead, about 400 injured, and more than 40,000 displaced, with Amatrice, Accumuli, and Arquata del Tronto among the hardest-hit. He prayed for victims and urged continued faith and solidarity to aid reconstruction.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱。教皇：国際社会は人命救助のために協力を

triage.notes: 記事にはCAR（金鉱山崩落）とイタリア中部地震への言及があるが、これらは疾病事象ではなく本イベント（エボラ）とは無関係。CARは対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。DRCのみを発生国として検証。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola: 'The epidemic is growing exponentially'
article.articleSummary: Through August 20, 2026, the DRC reports 5,375 confirmed Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases and 2,557 deaths (case fatality rate 47.6%). In the last 24 hours, 85 new confirmed cases were recorded in Ituri (63), North Kivu (17), and Haut-Uélé (5); 15 recoveries (Ituri 9, Haut-Uélé 4, North Kivu 2); and 23 deaths in Ebola Treatment Centers (Ituri 19, Haut-Uélé 2, Tshopo 1, North Kivu 1). Ituri remains epicenter with 83.9% of cumulative cases and 74.1% of new cases in the last day. Across six provinces, 56 of 151 health zones are affected. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no approved treatment or vaccine exists. Ervebo doses—16,250 in Kinshasa as part of a 70,000-dose package—have arrived, with more expected next week. Ring-vaccination trials with Ervebo are planned, though efficacy against Bundibugyo remains unproven. Three months in, 160 healthcare workers have contracted Ebola, 43 have died.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：「流行が指数関数的に拡大している」
triage.triage_reason: 確定症例5,375例・死亡2,557例（致死率47.6%）と大規模で急速に拡大しており、6州56保健地域に及び、承認済み治療薬・ワクチンが存在しないBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行であるためIHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: 医療従事者160名感染・43名死亡、致死率47.6%と非常に高く、承認薬・ワクチンが存在しないBundibugyoエボラウイルス株による流行。国際的なワクチン支援（Ervebo）が進行中であり、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Veja como é a 'vacina inteligente' contra a chikungunya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: See how the 'smart vaccine' against Chikungunya works.
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya vaccine innovation from the University of São Paulo (Ribeirão Preto) and University of Bonn (Germany) uses a genetically modified chikungunya virus that can replicate once but cannot mature into an infectious form. Reported in npj Vaccines, the strategy replaces the furin-cleavage site with a tobacco etch virus (TEV) protease site, and employs human cells lacking furin; TEV is absent in humans, so produced viruses remain immature after initial replication and serve as antigens. In mice, a single dose protected against chikungunya, and immunized animals also neutralized Mayaro virus, suggesting broader arboviral protection. The platform could be adapted to Zika, dengue, and yellow fever. It aims to be safer for immunocompromised and elderly individuals than current live-attenuated vaccines. Funded by FAPESP; collaboration with the University of Bonn; published 23 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: チクングニアに対する『スマートワクチン』の仕組みとは

triage.notes: 本記事はサンパウロ大学とボン大学によるチクングニアワクチン開発の研究報告であり、疾病発生・流行に関する内容ではない。ブラジルは研究実施地として言及されているが、感染症イベントの発生地ではないため対象国リストには含めない。

The article underscores the ongoing Ebola threat in the DRC and public health urgency, highlighting religious leadership urging coordinated prevention and protection of affected communities.

article.articleHeadline: بابا الفاتيكان يحث العالم على التحرك لمواجهة إيبولا في الكونجو الديمقراطية - بوابة الشروق

article.articleHeadline: दिल्ली में तेजी से बढ़े H1N1 के मामले, क्या नया स्ट्रेन है वजह? ICMR ने दिया जवाब
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: H1N1 cases have surged rapidly in Delhi; is a new strain the cause? ICMR has provided the answer.
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports a surge in H1N1 cases amid a seasonal rise in influenza across India. ICMR scientists say there is no new strain; the circulating virus is Influenza A H1N1 pdm09, strain A/Missouri/11/2025, in circulation since 2025 and aligning with the northern hemisphere vaccine strain. In Delhi this year, 2,392 Influenza-A cases have been recorded, of which 1,777 are H1N1; last year at this time, 229 H1N1 cases were reported; total influenza cases in the city exceed 2,600. Factors include higher humidity during monsoon, temperature changes, and crowded households. Category A cases with mild symptoms can be managed at home with isolation; high-risk groups (pregnant women, those over 65, young children, and people with comorbidities) may receive antivirals. Alarm signs—shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, lethargy, vomiting/diarrhea, coughing blood—require hospital care. Delhi has 35 hospitals under surveillance; AIIMS and NCDC testing active; adequate beds, oxygen, medicines, and ventilators. Published 2026-08-23.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1症例が急増、新しい株が原因か？ICMRが回答

triage.notes: 既知の季節性H1N1株による症例増加であり、ICMR・AIIMS・NCDCが監視・対応中。病床・酸素・薬剤・人工呼吸器は十分とされ、外部支援の必要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Bali Assures Travel Safety Amid Zika Virus Fears
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-23, Zika fears prompt a US CDC Level 2 Travel Health Notice for Indonesia, specifically Bali, issued Aug 7, 2026. Bali authorities report no Zika infections detected or reported to date. Tourism officials reassure visitors Bali remains safe, urging continued vigilance against mosquito-borne diseases, including Zika and dengue; preventive measures to avoid Aedes bites are emphasized for tourists and service providers. Zika infection generally causes mild or no symptoms, but poses pregnancy-related risks such as birth defects. The alert follows reports of Zika cases among travelers returning from Bali, indicating imported exposure rather than local spread. Bali’s tourism continues to rise, with 4.68 million international arrivals Jan–Apr 2026, up 8.24% year-on-year. Health offices advocate ongoing health standards, cleanliness, and mosquito-control measures.

triage.headline_ja: バリ島、ジカウイルスへの懸念の中で渡航の安全性を保証

article.articleHeadline: OMS alerta para avanço do Ebola e diz que epidemia ainda está longe de ser controlada
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warns of the spread of Ebola and says the outbreak is still far from being under control.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, the World Health Organization warns that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains far from under control, with ongoing risk of cross-border spread. Congolese authorities report over 2,300 deaths and about 5,000 confirmed cases, making this the deadliest outbreak in the country’s recent history. The epidemic is concentrated in the central-northern and eastern DRC, intensified by fragile governance and limited health infrastructure that impede case identification, patient isolation, and contact tracing. The WHO classifies the public health risk as very high in the DRC and high in Uganda and neighboring countries; global risk is currently low but could rise if transmission extends. Uganda and adjacent nations have heightened surveillance to prevent cross-border transmission. The outbreak had already been declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) three months earlier, underscoring the need for a strengthened international response focused on surveillance and containment.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇レオ14世、コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ出血熱の封じ込め強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で「同国史上最も致死的」とされるエボラ出血熱の流行が拡大しており、数千人の死者と脆弱な保健インフラ・武装勢力による混乱が重なり、IHR基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響・異常性）を2つ以上満たすためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はローマ教皇による国際社会への支援要請に基づく報道であり、具体的な症例数・検査確認データ・感染源等の詳細情報は含まれていない。バチカンは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: No new strain of H1N1 detected in India, says ICMR
article.articleSummary: India’s Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) confirms no new Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strain detected in the country. The circulating H1N1 variant since 2025 matches this year’s vaccine formulation. ICMR specifies that the Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses in circulation belong to the A/Missouri/11/2025(H1N1)pdm09-like strain. The statement coincides with rising flu cases in Delhi and reflects ongoing laboratory confirmation and strain monitoring within India. This finding suggests absence of a novel variant and alignment with the seasonal vaccine, with authorities continuing surveillance. No exact case counts, infection sources, or information on imported/exported cases are provided in the report. Published date: 2026-08-23.

triage.headline_ja: インドで新型H1N1株は検出されず、ICMRが発表
triage.triage_reason: ICMRは新規変異株の出現を否定しており、既存の季節性インフルエンザ株がワクチン株と一致していることを確認する内容で、異常性や重大なリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: デリーでのインフルエンザ症例増加に言及があるが、これは季節性インフルエンザの通常の流行を示すものであり、新規株の出現や異常事態は否定されている。

article.articleHeadline: وزير الصحة يؤكد التزام مصر بدعم الأمن الصحي الأفريقي ويدعو لتعزيز الاستعداد للأوبئة - اليوم السابع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Minister of Health affirms Egypt's commitment to supporting Africa's health security and calls for strengthening preparedness for epidemics - The Seventh Day
article.articleSummary: Egyptian Minister of Health and Population and co-chair of Africa’s High-Level Committee on Reforming the Global Health Architecture reaffirmed Egypt’s steadfast support for African countries facing shared health challenges and called for stronger epidemic preparedness. Speaking via video conference at the committee meeting with the Africa CDC Director General and African health ministers, he expressed solidarity with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, praising frontline workers confronting Ebola outbreaks and other epidemics. He urged Africa to move from reactive aid to sustainable readiness, noting epidemic responses test the global health framework and require rapid, coordinated action to save lives. He backed Africa-led clinical trials and evidence generation, and urged sustainable, predictable financing, including reforms to World Bank and multilateral development bank funding. He supported equitable pathogen access and benefit-sharing, rapid genomic data sharing, and technology transfer, arguing Africa must lead future global health governance.

triage.headline_ja: 保健相、アフリカの保健安全保障支援へのエジプトの関与を確認し、疫病への備え強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 記事はエジプト保健相による外交的声明であり、DRC・ウガンダでの既存エボラ流行への言及にとどまり、新規の疫学的情報は含まれていないため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ流行の新規情報ではなく、アフリカの保健安全保障強化に関する外交的声明。ウガンダも言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。エジプトも対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: البابا يدعو إلى تكثيف جهود احتواء تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديموقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope calls for intensified efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-23, the Pope called on the international community to intensify efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak is described as the deadliest in the nation's history, with thousands of deaths and ongoing spread in northern and eastern provinces marked by weak health infrastructure and armed conflict. The Pope urged preventive actions to save lives and expressed solidarity with those affected. The article does not provide precise case counts, laboratory confirmation details, or infection sources. It frames the crisis within broader humanitarian challenges while stressing global public-health support and local measures to curb transmission and protect vulnerable populations in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ流行封じ込め努力の強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で「同国史上最悪」とされるエボラ流行が継続し、多数の死者と武力紛争下での脆弱な医療体制が報告されており、国際的関心・支援要請も高いためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は具体的な症例数や検査確認情報を提供していないが、教皇による国際的な呼びかけという社会的関心の高さと、既知の大規模流行状況から重大性が示唆される。続報での正確な疫学データ確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, l'appello di Leone XIV: "In Congo troppe vittime, il mondo intervenga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, Leo XIV's appeal: "In the Congo, too many victims; the world must intervene."
article.articleSummary: As of 23 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains deadly, with Pope Leo XIV appealing to the international community to intervene. Speaking during the Angelus from St. Peter's Square, the Pope urged a response that directly involves local communities in prevention efforts to salvage as many lives as possible. The appeal underscores the ongoing Ebola epidemic in the DRC and its toll on victims. In a separate note, the Pope also addressed the Central African Republic, struck by a mine collapse in Zamboye, calling for improved safety and rule-of-law in mining sites. The remarks emphasize global solidarity and community-level preventive actions as key to containment of Ebola in the Congo while drawing attention to regional mining safety concerns.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ、レオ14世の訴え:「コンゴで犠牲者があまりに多い、世界は介入すべきだ」
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ流行が深刻な死者を出しており、ローマ教皇が国際社会に介入を呼びかけるなど社会的関心も高いため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は主にコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行への教皇の訴えを扱っている。中央アフリカ共和国の鉱山崩落事故は別件でエボラとは無関係のため対象外。バチカンは対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Plus de 2 500 morts : la progression d'Ebola inquiète
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 2,500 dead: the progression of Ebola is worrying.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-23, the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest and deadliest Ebola virus disease episode the country has faced. More than 2,500 deaths have been recorded, with more cases and deaths in three months than during the last Ebola wave, which lasted two years. The country has recently received vaccines, but their effectiveness against this strain is unknown. United Nations officials say the resources deployed are no longer sufficient to curb the exponential progression of the disease. The report underscores the urgent need for expanded vaccination, increased treatment capacity, and enhanced public health measures to prevent further spread. Outbreak management remains urgent.

triage.headline_ja: 2500人以上死亡：エボラの拡大が懸念される
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最大・最悪のエボラ流行で死者2500人超、国連が現行対応の不足を指摘しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生イベント。
triage.notes: 過去最大規模の流行で3ヶ月の症例・死亡数が前回2年間の流行を上回るとされ、既存ワクチンの当該株への有効性も不明であり、国際支援の緊急拡大が必要とされている。

article.articleHeadline: Папа Лав Четрнаести апеловао на помоћ Конгу због епидемије еболе
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pope Leo XIV appealed for aid to Congo because of the Ebola epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (Bundibugyo strain) continues in the Democratic Republic of Congo with spillover into Uganda; WHO declared a regional Ebola outbreak in May 2026. As of August 23, 2026, total confirmed cases reach 5,300 with more than 2,500 deaths. There is no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo Ebola currently. The outbreak's spread is hampered by armed conflict between government forces and armed groups in the major cities where cases cluster. Pope Leo XIV called for an international response focused on prevention and local community engagement to save lives during Sunday prayers in Vatican. Separately, he prayed for victims of a mining disaster in the Central African Republic; more than 100 people died on August 18 in a landslide at a surface gold mine in Zambia, with authorities noting the site had been closed prior to the incident.

triage.headline_ja: レオ14世教皇、エボラ流行によりコンゴへの支援を訴える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生中のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）はウガンダへの越境を伴い、確定症例5,300人・死者2,500人超と極めて深刻で、WHOが地域規模の流行を宣言済みであり、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境（スピルオーバー）が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ザンビア・中央アフリカ共和国での鉱山事故（土砂崩れ）はエボラとは別事案であり、ザンビアは対象国だがエボラ発生国ではないため除外した。有効なワクチン・治療法が未承認である点、武力紛争により対応が困難な点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Rugăciunile Papei pentru populațiile greu încercate de epidemia de Ebola și de alte tragedii
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope's prayers for populations hard-hit by the Ebola epidemic and other tragedies.
article.articleSummary: Pope Francis urges active international engagement to combat the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo, emphasizing prevention and the involvement of local communities to save lives amid the outbreak. The appeal, voiced after the Sunday Angelus in St. Peter's Square on 23 August 2026, also expresses solidarity with the Central African Republic's population mourning a mining-site collapse at Zamboyé, praying for the dead and for safety and legitimacy in mining operations. The Holy Father marks the forthcoming tenth anniversary of the 24 August 2016 Central Italy earthquake affecting Lazio, Umbria, and Marche, praying for victims’ families and ongoing reconstruction. The article does not provide Ebola case or death counts. The piece frames a broader humanitarian response spanning Africa’s health crises and Italy’s disaster recovery.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、エボラ出血熱やその他の悲劇に苦しむ人々のために祈りを捧げる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のエボラ出血熱流行について教皇が国際的な関与を呼びかけており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大の懸念）を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は教皇による祈りと国際的関与の呼びかけが主題であり、感染者数・死者数などの疫学データは提供されていない。中央アフリカ共和国の鉱山事故やイタリア地震は別事象であり、エボラの発生国はDRCのみ確認される。

article.articleHeadline: وزير الصحة يؤكد التزام مصر بدعم الأمن الصحي الإفريقي ويدعو لتعزيز الاستعداد القاري لمواجهة الأوبئة - بوابة الشروق
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health Minister affirms Egypt's commitment to supporting African health security and calls for strengthening continental preparedness to confront epidemics.
article.articleSummary: Egyptian Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar reiterated Egypt’s support for African countries in strengthening health security and preparedness to confront epidemics. Speaking via video conference at the African Ministers’ meeting of the high-level committee on reforming the global health architecture, he conveyed solidarity with the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda and commended frontline workers combating Ebola and other outbreaks. He urged Africa to move from reactive aid to sustainable preparedness with built-in capabilities and solutions, noting that the current pandemic response tests the global health system and resilience lies in rapid, coordinated action. He endorsed Africa-led clinical trials and generation of evidence, and stressed pre-existing research capacity. He linked outbreak readiness to sustainable funding and reform discussions on World Bank and multilateral banks, emphasizing equitable access to countermeasures, timely pathogen genomics sharing, and technology transfer as core to trust. He urged Africa to lead health governance in the future.

triage.headline_ja: 保健相、アフリカの健康安全保障支援へのエジプトの関与を確認、大陸レベルの疫病対応準備強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: エジプト保健相の外交的声明記事であり、DRC・ウガンダでのエボラ対応への言及はあるが新規の感染拡大情報や具体的な症例数などのデータは含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事はエジプト保健相の会議発言に関する外交的内容が主であり、DRCにおける既存のエボラ流行への言及にとどまる。新規感染データなし。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。継続的な情報収集が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Moçambique em alerta máximo face à epidemia de Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mozambique on high alert in the face of the Ebola epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Mozambique is on maximum alert for an Ebola epidemic in Central Africa, acting as a transit corridor for foreign nationals seeking to reach other destinations through Mozambican territory. As of 23 August 2026, Mozambique has not recorded any Ebola cases. Health Minister Ussene Isse cautions that concern is rising daily and notes the current cold season brings more influenza-like and respiratory infections, underscoring the need to maintain prevention measures for flu and respiratory illnesses. The country has strengthened border surveillance along the Mozambique–Tanzania border due to substantial mobility from the Democratic Republic of Congo toward Tanzania, and travel flows from nearby countries such as Uganda via airports. Citizens are urged to seek medical care at the first signs of Ebola symptoms—high fever, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal and joint pains. Emphasis remains on vigilant surveillance and adherence to public health recommendations to prevent introduction.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行を前にモザンビークが最高警戒態勢
triage.triage_reason: 記事はモザンビーク国内での警戒態勢強化を報じているが、モザンビーク自体では症例は確認されておらず、中央アフリカ（DRC等）での実際の流行状況について詳細情報が不足しているため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はモザンビークの越境警戒態勢であり、モザンビーク自体はエボラ未発生（対象国リストにも含まれない）。DRCは移動元として言及されているが、DRC国内での具体的な症例数・流行規模の情報は本記事にはない。続報でDRCでの実際の発生状況を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Pope appeals for int'l solidarity as deadly Ebola outbreak spreads
article.articleSummary: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO faces a deadly Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain. World Health Organization data released this past week show the outbreak on track to surpass the 2014–2016 epidemic, the deadliest on record. About 5,300 confirmed cases have been reported, with more than 2,500 fatalities among them. The Bundibugyo strain is rare and has no approved treatments. Officials believe the virus began spreading months before detection, possibly as early as February, with official declaration in May. Ongoing transmission is hampered by armed conflict in cities where the outbreak is concentrated, complicating contact tracing and control efforts. Pope Leo XIV appealed for international solidarity and local prevention efforts in St. Peter’s Square, urging a global and community response to save lives. The report relies on WHO data from the past week.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、致死的なエボラ出血熱の流行拡大を受け国際的連帯を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でBundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱が拡大し、2014-2016年の大流行を超える規模（確定5,300例、死亡2,500例超）に達しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にVatican Cityが含まれるが、これは教皇の発言拠点であり実際の感染発生国ではないため除外。武力紛争地域での感染拡大により接触者追跡が困難化しており、既知株ながら治療薬未承認で致死率が高い点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: البابا يدعو لإنقاذ الكونغو الديمقراطية من "إيبولا" ويعزي...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope calls to save the Democratic Republic of the Congo from Ebola and offers condolences...
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the northern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is ongoing as of 23 August 2026, with the Pope urging international and local action to contain transmission and save lives. The report notes severe spread in regions with weak health infrastructure and security disruptions linked to armed groups. It provides no case counts, laboratory confirmation details, or infection source in the article. The Pope also offered condolences for victims of a mining disaster in the Central African Republic near the Cameroon border and called for enhanced safety and compliance in mining operations. The focus remains on reinforced surveillance and preventive measures to curb Ebola spread in the affected DRC regions.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、エビデミック「エボラ」からコンゴ民主共和国を救うよう呼びかけ、哀悼の意を表す
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国北部・東部でエボラ出血熱の流行が継続中であり、脆弱な保健インフラと武装勢力による治安悪化が絡む深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であるため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は主にコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行に焦点を当てている。中央アフリカ共和国・カメルーン国境付近の鉱山事故への言及はエボラとは別の出来事であり、対象国リストにも該当しないため除外した。具体的な症例数や検査確定情報は記事に記載なし。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A
Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: स्वाइन फ्लू को लेकर ICMR का बड़ा बयान, देश में नहीं मिला कोई नया वेरिएंट, जानिए कहां बढ़ रहे H1N1 के मरीज?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: ICMR's major statement on swine flu: No new variant detected in the country, find out where H1N1 patients are rising.
article.articleSummary: ICMR states no new dangerous H1N1 (influenza A) variant detected in India; the circulating influenza-A H1N1 pdm09 is an existing strain and has been present since 2025. The current virus matches the seasonal flu vaccine; no cause for widespread panic, though children and the elderly may experience worse symptoms. Seek medical care if symptoms persist 3–4 days or breathing difficulties arise. Delhi reports 2,392 influenza-A cases, including 1,777 H1N1, with hospitals advised to stay vigilant and equipped. In Chhattisgarh, 38 confirmed swine flu cases, majority in Raipur (25) and others in Bilaspur, Durg, Balodabazar, Bastar, Bemetara, Raigarh, prompting state alerts. Madhya Pradesh sees rising activity, with a death in Ujjain; 5-day data show four cases across Indore and Ujjain, and three confirmed on Saturday in separate cities. Common symptoms: fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, fatigue; transmission mainly via respiratory droplets.

triage.headline_ja: スワインフルーに関するICMRの重要声明：国内で新変異株は検出されず、H1N1患者が増加している地域は？
triage.triage_reason: ICMRは新規変異株の検出はなく既存の季節性H1N1株であると明言しており、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、複数州で症例増加・死亡例が報告されており継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: ICMRは既存株であり新変異株ではないと強調し「パニックの必要なし」としているが、デリー、チャッティースガル、マディヤ・プラデーシュ州で症例増加・死亡例（ウッジャイン）が報告されている。季節性インフルエンザの通常の活動増加とみられ、フルRRAの緊急性は低いが今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: بابا الفاتيكان يدعو لتكثيف جهود احتواء تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديموقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope calls for intensified efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of August 23, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo—the deadliest in the country’s history—has claimed thousands of lives and is spreading across northern and eastern provinces amid weak health infrastructure and ongoing armed-group violence. Health authorities warn the outbreak is accelerating, complicating containment efforts. The World Health Organization has warned about the rapid progression of Ebola and response challenges. The Pope, speaking from St. Peter’s Square, urged intensified international and local action to prevent transmission and save lives. The appeal highlights the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, community engagement, and resources to bolster prevention and response in affected communities.

triage.headline_ja: ローマ教皇、コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ出血熱の流行封じ込めへの取り組み強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最悪規模とされるエボラ流行が拡大しており、WHOも警告を発している。公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクがありIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: バチカンは発生地域ではなく、教皇の発言の場所であるため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola au Haut-Uele : les communautés s'engagent à contribuer à la lutte contre l'épidémie - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Haut-Uele: communities commit to contribute to the fight against the outbreak - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Haut-Uele, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, spurred a broad community mobilization. On 23 August 2026 in Isiro, communities and provincial authorities pledged to pool resources and intensify risk communication to break the transmission chain. Governor Jean Bakomito announced commitments from civil society, national and provincial lawmakers, youth and women’s groups, public and private service leaders, and religious authorities to drive a community-led response. He cited central government support, including three ambulances recently dispatched by President Félix Tshisekedi’s Task-Force, with medicines and funds arriving to strengthen the response. The gathering took place at the multipurpose hall of the governor’s official residence in Isiro’s Kupa district. The event emphasizes community engagement as a key element in outbreak containment.

triage.headline_ja: オー・ウエレ州のエボラ:地域社会が流行対策への貢献を約束 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR基準に該当する重大疾患であり、DRC北東部で継続中のアウトブレイクに対する地域社会動員が報じられている。国際的拡大・渡航貿易制限のリスクを有するためフルRRA対象とする。
triage.notes: 記事は地域社会・行政・大統領府タスクフォースによる対応強化を報じており、継続中のエボラ流行の一環と考えられる。感染者数・死亡者数など詳細な疫学データは記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : 75 leaders religieux protestants et musulmans mobilisés contre Ebola à Bunia - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: 75 Protestant and Muslim religious leaders mobilized to fight Ebola in Bunia - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola response in Bunia, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo: Seventy-five religious leaders from Protestant and Muslim communities in the Bunia health zone were mobilized to strengthen community engagement in the Ebola response. The National Public Health Institute (INSP), via its Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COUSP) and with UNICEF funding, organized a briefing to promote prevention measures and counter misinformation. Leaders were urged to serve as trusted relay points to share reliable information, address public concerns, and foster protective behaviors. The participants pledged to mobilize their congregations to support the response and to reinforce trust between communities and medical teams, a critical strategy for rumor control in a region where misinformation can hinder the fight against Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州:ブニアでのエボラ対策のためプロテスタントとイスラム教指導者75名が動員 - ACP

article.articleHeadline: दिल्ली में H1N1 के बीच बढ़ी कोविड निगरानी, अस्पतालों को जांच और रिपोर्टिंग तेज करने के निर्देश - delhi intensifies covid19 surveillance amid rising h1n1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Delhi intensifies COVID-19 surveillance amid rising H1N1.
article.articleSummary: As of August 23, 2026, Delhi tightens COVID-19 surveillance amid rising H1N1 activity. COVID testing is now mandatory for all SARIs (severe acute respiratory infections), with ILI (influenza-like illness) cases also under COVID surveillance. Hospitals report into the IDSP–IHIP Integrated Health Information Platform, per central guidance. A 2025 directive mandated COVID testing for all SARIs and 5% of ILIs, with regular data uploads. Testing uses RT-PCR; SARS-CoV-2 genome is identified in COVID tests, while influenza A is identified in H1N1 diagnosis; multiplex RT-PCR can detect influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2 from a single sample. For severe SARIs, hospitals must ensure oxygen and ventilation; rapid-response teams may be deployed for unusual spikes. Authorities stress this is heightened surveillance, not a new wave, aimed at early detection of spikes in H1N1, COVID, and other respiratory infections.

triage.headline_ja: デリー、H1N1増加に伴いCOVID-19監視を強化 病院に検査・報告の迅速化を指示

triage.notes: 既存の季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1）増加に伴う既存プロトコルに基づくサーベイランス強化であり、新規シグナルとしての重要性は低い。当局は『新しい波ではなく早期発見のための措置』と明言している。

article.articleHeadline: Kwango : le choléra progresse à Kasongo-Lunda, déjà 560 cas notifiés et 37 décès (Par Héritier Matenga) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kwango: Cholera spreads to Kasongo-Lunda, already 560 reported cases and 37 deaths (By Héritier Matenga) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreaks in Kasongo-Lunda health zone, Kwango province, southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 560 cases and 37 deaths reported as of 23 August 2026. The outbreak spreads despite government interventions; 37 fatalities reported since August 17 amid stockouts and limited adherence to preventive measures by communities. Angola-imported cases contribute to the spread. Kasongo-Lunda now the active epidemic hotspot. Response challenges include no morgue, unsafe handling of 37 corpses, and lack of transport for community workers (motorbikes/bicycles) hindering case detection, water treatment distribution, and sample transport to Kenge laboratory, delaying laboratory confirmation. Critical stockouts of rehydration solutes, medicines, and PPE, with supplies already shared to Popokabaka. Severe water scarcity and rural isolation worsen transmission. Urgent, coordinated action is needed from central government, Health Ministry, provincial authorities, WHO, and partners (Memisa Belgium, MSF, LDS Church) to replenish stocks, provide transport, secure corpse management, and ensure potable water access.

triage.headline_ja: クワンゴ州:コレラがカソンゴ・ルンダに拡大、既に560件の症例と37人の死亡が報告(著者:エリティエ・マテンガ)-ACP

article.articleHeadline: Papa pede oração contra Ebola: o que se sabe sobre o surto
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pope Calls for Prayers Against Ebola: What Is Known About the Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has grown, with 2,516 deaths reported by the CDC as of August 20, 2026. The infection is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no vaccines or specific treatments. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC and has surpassed 1,000 cases about 40 days after the response began, faster than the 2018 outbreak, which took about 235 days to exceed 1,000. The outbreak affects northeastern DRC and has reached Kampala, Uganda. In Uganda, there are 20 cases and 2 deaths; no sustained community transmission; the most recent confirmed case was June 21 and linked to travel from the DRC. Pope Leo XIV, at the Angelus in St. Peter's Square on Aug 23, called for prayers and international action focused on prevention to save lives in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 教皇、エボラ出血熱に対する祈りを呼びかけ：アウトブレイクについて分かっていること

article.articleHeadline: Papa pozvao na akciju: Ebola u Kongu odnijela više od 2.500 života
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Pope called for action: Ebola in the Congo has claimed more than 2,500 lives.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the 17th Ebola outbreak, now the country’s deadliest, with more than 2,500 deaths and over 4,200 confirmed cases in Ituri province, and spread to six of 26 provinces across the north and east. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain lacks approved vaccines or therapies; however, Ervebo vaccine doses will be used in a trial—20,000 for efficacy testing against Bundibugyo and 50,000 for frontline health workers. The epidemic, declared three months ago, has expanded rapidly, with half of the roughly 2,500 deaths occurring in the last 20 days. Health workers in Bunia report unpaid salaries (about 160 infected and 43 deaths among staff), while attacks, misinformation, and community distrust hinder the response. Uganda reported 20 cases and 2 deaths and declared Ebola-free on July 28. The Pope called for international action and inclusion of local communities in prevention efforts.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Don't ignore swine flu symptoms; keep these things in mind.

Practice good hygiene: cover coughs/sneezes with tissue, dispose correctly, wash hands frequently with soap and water, and use hand sanitizer. Published 23 August 2026.

article.articleHeadline: 'No cause for panic': ICMR says no new H1N1 strain detected, urges caution for high-risk groups
article.articleSummary: India's ICMR reports no new H1N1 strain circulating; current Influenza A (H1N1) pdm09 viruses in India are the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like strain, clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, circulating since 2025, with surveillance ongoing and no panic warranted. Symptoms include fever, cough, headache, and body ache; most cases are self-limiting, but young children, the elderly, and those with underlying conditions require caution and timely medical consultation if symptoms persist. Amid rising cases, Delhi issued a public health advisory on respiratory hygiene, masking in crowded places, and seeking care for flu-like symptoms, including covering coughs and handwashing. Delhi has logged over 1,777 H1N1 cases this year, with 114 new cases reported on Thursday and total Influenza-A cases exceeding 2,300. article.articleHeadline: Chikungunya Raises New Concerns Over Blood Transfusion Safety
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya (CHIKV), a mosquito-borne illness causing fever and severe joint pain, may threaten blood safety as outbreaks expand. The virus has been reported in more than 110 countries across Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Europe. Donors can be viremic even when asymptomatic: CHIKV RNA positivity around 0.5% overall, about 0.6% in endemic/outbreak settings, with higher rates of 1.9% in Puerto Rico and 1% in Thailand and French Polynesia. In Puerto Rico’s peak months, viral RNA was found in 1.34% of donors, with some very high viral loads. Lab studies show infectious CHIKV can survive routine blood processing, recovered from red cells, platelets, and plasma; however, this does not prove transmission. Clinically verified transfusion transmissions are extremely limited, so current risk is very low but not zero. Safeguards include NAAT screening and pathogen-reduction, not universally available. Italian institutions—Pisa, Rome’s Lazzaro Spallanzani, Mantua—contributed; findings published in Viruses.

triage.headline_ja: チクングニア熱、輸血の安全性に対する新たな懸念を提起
triage.triage_reason: 特定の国・地域における新規アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、チクングニアウイルスの輸血感染リスクに関する研究レビュー記事であり、シグナルとして扱う具体的な公衆衛生イベントが確認できない。
triage.notes: 本記事はイタリアの研究機関（ピサ、ローマ、マントヴァ）による国際的な文献レビュー（Viruses誌掲載）であり、タイやプエルトリコ等のドナー陽性率データは既存研究の引用に過ぎず、特定国での新規アウトブレイクを報じるものではない。そのためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: दिल्ली में फैल रहा H1N1 वायरस कितना खतरनाक? डॉक्टर से जानें क्यों बढ़ रहे स्वाइन फ्लू के केस
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How dangerous is the H1N1 virus spreading in Delhi? Learn from a doctor why swine flu cases are on the rise.
article.articleSummary: H1N1 (swine flu) cases are rising in Delhi-NCR. The virus is mutating, with antigenic drift producing new variants that can better evade existing immunity from vaccines or prior infections. Dr. Randeep Guleria, former AIIMS director, notes such mutations are normal, and while they raise concern, panic is not advised. Environmental factors like rain and humidity extend viral survival, aiding transmission. Most people recover, but the elderly and those with underlying illnesses are more likely to require ICU care. H1N1 primarily affects the respiratory system and spreads via coughing and sneezing. Symptoms include shortness of breath, dry cough, runny nose, body and head aches, sore throat, fever, chills, and weakness. Seek medical attention if breathing becomes difficult, confusion occurs, there is persistent high fever, or blue lips. Preventive steps include covering coughs and sneezes, washing hands, avoiding public places when coughing/fever, staying hydrated, eating well, and resting.

triage.headline_ja: デリーで拡大するH1N1ウイルスの危険性とは？医師に聞く、なぜ豚インフルエンザの症例が増加しているのか

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Records 1,777 H1N1 Cases This Year; ICMR Says No New Strain, No Cause For Panic
article.articleSummary: Delhi has recorded 1,777 H1N1 influenza cases this year, with 114 new cases on August 20, among a total of 2,602 seasonal influenza (Influenza A and B) cases cumulative through 2026. H1N1 now dominates Influenza A in Delhi, accounting for 1,777 of 2,392 Influenza A cases up to Aug 20, while H1 and H3 contributed 37 and 138 cases, respectively, and 440 were other Influenza A types; 210 Influenza B cases are also reported. ICMR scientists confirm no new H1N1 strain, identifying circulating A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like viruses (clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1) in circulation since 2025 and well matched to Northern Hemisphere vaccine strains; there is no cause for panic. Common symptoms include fever, cough, headache, and body ache; most cases are self-limiting, but young children, the elderly, and those with medical conditions require caution. Delhi enforces enhanced surveillance via IDSP-IHIP, with two national peaks typically Jan–Mar and post-monsoon. Public health measures include masks, respiratory hygiene, handwashing, and avoiding self-medication; alerts and training are ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: Amid week-long rain forecast in Telangana, Health department warns of rise in dengue, viral infections
article.articleSummary: Telangana's Health department warns of a rise in mosquito-borne illnesses amid a week-long forecast of light to moderate rainfall by IMD Hyderabad, with heavy rainfall alerts for several districts over the next three days. Preventive measures include using mosquito nets or screens, repellents, maintaining drains to prevent water stagnation, and covering septic tanks with mesh; residents are advised to observe a 'Friday-Dry Day' to eliminate standing water around homes. People with flu-like symptoms—cough with fever, headache, sore throat and body pains—should visit the nearest government health facility; 108 ambulance service is available for emergencies. Authorities have arranged special beds, intravenous fluids, and essential medicines at public facilities, with medicines and ORS sachets distributed to ANMs, ASHAs, and Anganwadi workers to meet exigencies.

The Pope’s remarks underscore the humanitarian and public health gravity of the Ebola crisis in the DRC and call for renewed international solidarity and support to curb transmission. The article provides limited detail beyond the death toll and does not mention laboratory confirmation, specific transmission chains, infection sources, or response measures. It emphasizes global public health action to address the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: レオ教皇、コンゴをエボラから救うため世界に緊急行動を呼びかける
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行で死者2,500人超と重大な公衆衛生上の影響があり、IHR基準の複数該当およびWPRO基準の該当により国際的関心も高い。
triage.notes: バチカン市国は発生地域として挙げられているが、これは教皇の発言場所であり実際の流行発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外。記事は死者数のみで検査確認や具体的な感染経路の詳細を欠く。
